Computation and Language.summary: Emotion classifiers are routinely applied beyond their training data, on the assumption that same-named labels such as fear or surprise mean the same thing across resources. We test this assumption for five labels shared by GoEmotions, XED, and BRIGHTER, comparing models on identical inputs and under cross-corpus transfer. On the same texts, one fear classifier flags 71% as fearful and another 8%, yet the two largely agree on how the texts rank. Across 30 resource-label comparisons, training-label prevalence explains about half of this kind of scale mismatch, and a fitted intercept removes most of it. What recalibration cannot repair is larger: transferred models lose 55% of native discrimination in aggregate, agreement in ranking between classifiers is only weakly related to that loss, and for surprise the resources disagree about which texts express the emotion. The choice of training resource can therefore change conclusions: on two external tweet collections, BRIGHTER- and XED-trained classifiers give opposite answers about which shows more surprise, even after rank normalization, with intervals excluding zero in both directions. A shared emotion label name does not establish an interchangeable measurement target.

Computation and Language.title: MS-GLA: Multi-Scale Gated Linear Attention for Addressing Representational Bottlenecks via Multi-Temporal Resolution
Computation and Language.summary: Gated Linear Attention (GLA) Transformers advance linear recurrent models through data-dependent gating, but face a core limitation: the fixed-capacity memory matrices across all heads operate at a single temporal resolution, where each token is processed individually, forcing them to simultaneously encode local syntactic patterns and long-range semantic structure, creating a representational bottleneck that gating alone is insufficient to resolve. We introduce Multi-Scale Gated Linear Attention (MS-GLA), which addresses this by distributing attention heads across multiple temporal resolutions. Coarser resolutions pool longer token spans naturally specializing toward long-range dependencies, while finer head groups retain sensitivity to local syntactic structure. A learnable, input-dependent fusion layer dynamically recombines head group outputs at each timestep, expanding effective memory capacity without increasing per-head state size. This multi-resolution decomposition draws on principles from Multi-Scale State-Space Models (MS-SSM), adapting them to the gated linear attention setting. We evaluate MS-GLA on language modeling, recall-intensive tasks, and long-context generalization. Across all settings, MS-GLA consistently achieves higher accuracy and lower perplexity than GLA at matched parameter counts, with up to 18.9% improvement on recall-intensive tasks and 9.5% lower average perplexity on language modeling benchmarks, validating multi-temporal resolution decomposition as a principled and effective extension of Gated Linear Attention.

Computation and Language.title: COFFEQA: Counterfactual-Guided Few-Shot Distillation for LLM Question Answering
Computation and Language.summary: Knowledge distillation aims to train a smaller student model to mimic a larger teacher model for resource-constrained environments. However, the process of distillation is typically data-intensive and computationally expensive, particularly for generative tasks. Few-shot distillation offers an alternative by transferring teacher knowledge using limited training samples. However, we observe that few-shot distillation performance is heavily dependent on the choice of these training samples. In fact, we demonstrate that using more uncertain samples near the teacher's decision boundary can significantly deteriorate distillation performance. Motivated by this observation, we propose Counterfactual-guided Few-shot Distillation in Open-book Question Answering (COFFEQA), a novel strategy that aptly uses counterfactuals to provide additional supervision around challenging factual samples. In the generative QA setting, we define a counterfactual as a minimally modified context that induces the teacher to change its response to an alternative answer. We provide geometric insights on how factual-counterfactual pairs can constrain the deviation between the teacher's and student's decision boundaries. We further introduce a new metric, Context Following Difficulty (CFD) that further validates counterfactuals prior to distillation based on agreement with the intended alternative answer and dependence on the modified context. COFFEQA uses CFD-validated factual-counterfactual pairs for few-shot distillation. Experiments across five in-domain and three out-of-domain QA benchmarks using T5 and Qwen2.5 families show that COFFEQA outperforms factual-only distillation baselines under the same few-shot budget. For instance, on TriviaQA, COFFEQA improves over the factual-only baseline by 8.77 average EM points and 9.98 average F1 points under the T5 setting with 32 few-shot pairs.

Computation and Language.title: When Charts Deceive Web Agents: A Paired Benchmark for Misleading Visualization-Grounded Tasks
Computation and Language.summary: Web agents increasingly browse, interpret, and act on web content on behalf of users. In many realistic workflows, however, the visual evidence they consume is not neutral: charts and dashboards can be misleading, shaping judgments without issuing any explicit malicious instruction. Unlike chart question answering, Web Agents treat charts as intermediate evidence whose misinterpretation can propagate into concrete downstream actions --- a reliability risk that remains underexplored. We introduce MisVisAgentBench, the first paired executable benchmark for evaluating how misleading visualizations affect Web Agent execution. It comprises 280 task instances in matched clean--misleading pairs that differ only in chart evidence. We further provide a diagnostic framework that isolates misleading-induced failures from baseline task difficulty (Zhu et al., 2025) and captures execution-level effects such as extra browsing steps and decision hesitation. Across thirteen vision-language Web Agents, replacing clean charts with misleading counterparts reduces the average task success rate by more than 34 percentage points. Moreover, these failures predominantly follow the targeted misleading action branch, suggesting that deceptive charts systematically redirect rather than randomly disrupt agent decisions. These results reveal that visualization robustness is a critical yet understudied dimension of Web Agent safety and reliability.

Information Retrieval.title: Can Language Models Play the Wikipedia Game?
Information Retrieval.summary: Language models increasingly support or automate information retrieval from document collections too large to index. This task is difficult when it requires specialist linguistic or scientific knowledge. We used the Wikipedia Game to test language models on an analogous information retrieval task. In the game, players must reach a target article using only article links. We compared sentence embedding models and LLMs across five Wikipedia languages and five academic-literature datasets. We construct very large local graphs of Wikipedia pages and of paper citations using OpenAlex and provide code to build and navigate them. This allows the study of language models' navigation capabilities without relying on third-party APIs. We compared the models with human and TF-IDF benchmarks. The Wikipedia Game format enables robust comparisons across techniques, languages, and domains. No model significantly outperformed humans, although the best models (GPT-o3 mini, GPT-4o, QwQ:32B, and DeepSeek-R1:70B) achieved comparable success. Performance and rankings varied across languages and topics, with implications for practitioners utilising these techniques.
Information Retrieval.comment: 64 pages (14-page main text, references and 16 appendices), 17 figures, 10 tables

Information Retrieval.title: RATED: Reliability-Aware AI Agent Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics
Information Retrieval.summary: As AI agents increasingly rely on external tools, accurate retrieval is essential for reliable behavior. Existing methods optimize semantic relevance but largely ignore tool availability during execution. To address this gap, we propose RATED (Reliability-Aware Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics), a retrieval framework that combines robust semantic matching with dynamic reliability adaptation. RATED employs a frozen dual-encoder with contrastive fine-tuning for semantic matching, and a lightweight contextual bandit module that re-ranks candidates based on real-time execution feedback. This design enables rapid adaptation to runtime tool failures without expensive model retraining. We introduce EcoAgent, a benchmark of 5,172 real-world tools and over 210,000 query-tool pairs for offline retrieval and dynamic reliability evaluation. Experimental results demonstrate that RATED achieves a 52.2% relative MRR improvement over the ToolLLM API retriever on real-world queries, and reduces fault selection rate from 86.2% to 2.9% under severe API outage scenarios with a 30% failure rate, while incurring negligible latency overhead of less than 1 ms over encode-only inference. The code and dataset are available at https://github.com/Elliotes/EcoAgent.

Information Retrieval.title: Tracing and Taming Hallucinated Terms via Subsequence-Association Filtering and Breadth-Aware Selection for LLM Query Expansion
Information Retrieval.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are now a standard source of query expansion terms but they hallucinate. They inject non existent entities and off-topic terms that add ranking noise and can hurt strong retrievers. Existing remedies such as corpus grounding, mutual verification and preference alignment treat hallucinated terms as an undifferentiated nuisance to be filtered by agreement heuristics, without a mechanistic account of why a given term appears or a principled criterion for how many terms to keep. We propose Subsequence-Association Filtered, breadth-aware query expansion (SAFE-QE), a training-free, retriever agnostic method that draws on the subsequence-association account of hallucination. We score each candidate expansion term by its corpus conditioned cross-context reproducibility, terms that reappear under randomised query contexts yet lack support in the pseudo-relevant set are flagged as products of dominant hallucinatory associations and down-weighted. Drawing on the characterisation of language generation as a trade-off between consistency (no hallucination) and breadth (coverage), we cast term selection as constrained coverage maximisation over the pseudo-relevant set, keeping a set that is approximately broad but consistent and stable across resampling. We also introduce the Hallucinated Expansion Term Rate, a query side faithfulness metric that counts injected expansion terms no relevant document supports. We evaluate our approach on benchmarked TREC and BEIR collections. Our SAFE-QE is statistically indistinguishable from generative and corpus-steered expansion on nDCG@10 while injecting fewer unsupported terms 4.3 per query against 27.8 for Query2doc and 57.5 for HyDE and on a strong learned sparse retriever, where every expansion method regresses. Faithfulness is therefore available at no measurable cost in ranking quality.

Information Retrieval.title: Access Paths for Efficient Ordering with Large Language Models
Information Retrieval.summary: In this work, we present the \texttt{LLM ORDER BY} semantic operator as a logical abstraction and conduct a systematic study of its physical implementations. First, we propose several improvements to existing semantic sorting algorithms and introduce a semantic-aware external merge sort algorithm. Our extensive evaluation reveals that no single implementation offers universal optimality on all datasets. From our evaluations, we observe a general scaling relationship between sorting cost and the ordering quality for comparison-based algorithms. Building on these insights, we design a budget-aware optimizer that utilizes heuristic rules, LLM-as-Judge evaluation, and consensus aggregation to dynamically select the near-optimal access path for LLM ORDER BY. In our extensive evaluations, our optimizer consistently achieves ranking accuracy on par with or superior to the best static methods across all benchmarks. We believe that this work provides foundational insights into the principled optimization of semantic operators essential for building robust, large-scale LLM-powered analytic systems.

Information Retrieval.title: SPARQL-LLM in the TEXT2SPARQL 2026 Challenge
Information Retrieval.summary: Querying distributed data represented as Knowledge Graphs (KGs) via SPARQL remains a difficult task, requiring fluency in query syntax, endpoint specifications, and schema details. Knowledge Graph Question Answering (KGQA) systems address this by automatically translating natural language into SPARQL, and recent advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) have made this translation increasingly feasible. In this paper, we describe SPARQL-LLM, our open-source KGQA system, in the context of the TEXT2SPARQL 2026 challenge. In this challenge, SPARQL-LLM ranks first overall among eight competing approaches across all datasets, achieving up to 59% higher accuracy than the second-best approach and supporting multilingual question answering in English, German, and Spanish. SPARQL-LLM is publicly released at https://github.com/sib-swiss/sparql-llm and deployed in production over decentralized bioinformatics KGs at https://www.expasy.org/chat.

Information Retrieval.title: Beyond Temporal Proximity: Explanatory World Models for Credit Assignment in Reinforcement Learning
Information Retrieval.summary: Generative Recommenders increasingly use Reinforcement Learning (RL) to optimize outcomes that may appear hundreds or thousands of interactions after a decision. Standard RL propagates reward according to temporal proximity rather than explicit relevance, attenuating the signal assigned to distant but important actions and creating a source of sample inefficiency. We introduce Explanatory World Models (EWM), an attribution framework that uses explanations to identify the earlier events that plausibly contributed to a realized outcome. We instantiate EWM with a frontier language model and use its explanations as learning signals using a conservative hierarchical operator that recursively redistributes reward while preserving the undiscounted episode return. To investigate what constitutes a useful explanation, we operationalize three complementary variants inspired by Halpern's actual causation, Lombrozo's explanatory simplicity, and Deutsch's hard-to-vary explanations. We evaluate EWM on two controlled long-horizon RL benchmarks, a public sequential-recommendation benchmark, and an industry-scale generative recommender. On Crafter and WordCraft, EWM substantially outperforms PPO and LaRe, with its largest gains when rewards are most delayed. On KuaiRand, EWM outperforms SFT and LaRe offline and A2C online. Finally, in an offline evaluation of an industry generative recommender, EWM considerably improves Recall and increases behavioral proxies. These results suggest that explanations can provide structured and reusable credit for learning from delayed outcomes.

Information Retrieval.title: Web$hell: A Unified Interface for Agentic Web Access
Information Retrieval.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents are becoming direct users of the open web. As they take on increasingly complex and information-intensive tasks, effective web access is becoming a core capability for agentic problem solving. Existing approaches have advanced agentic web access through different access models, including search-augmented agents, browser-based agents, and, more recently, filesystem-based agents. Nevertheless, as users expect agents to complete long-horizon, end-to-end tasks, they increasingly need to conduct broad information gathering, perform browser actions, and revisit acquired evidence within a single trajectory. Yet our preliminary analyses reveal that existing access models struggle to meet these demands. They primarily support either information gathering or browser interaction, while combining their capabilities can involve substantial costs or performance trade-offs. To this end, we present Web\$hell, an interface that unifies web access under a single access model. Using a common schema defined by WebContract, WebCompiler compiles live webpages into addressable information and action objects. These objects are maintained in WebCache and handled through a shared set of operations, providing agents with consistent, operable, and persistent web access. Through extensive experiments across web search, web navigation, and deep research benchmarks, we show that Web\$hell achieves strong task performance at lower cost. Our results further indicate the importance of interface design for effective web access, with Web\$hell opening new possibilities for more capable and efficient LLM agents on the web.

Information Retrieval.title: NEAR: Neighborhood-Aware Residuals for Memory Retrieval
Information Retrieval.summary: Memory retrieval aims to identify evidence from stored records to answer a query. Stored records with different factual details may share topics, entities, or events. Such shared contents would make records without the required evidence more likely to receive high similarity scores and outrank the correct evidence. In this paper, we use the information shared by these records to construct local references for query-memory matching. We propose NEighborhood-Aware Residuals (NEAR), a training-free framework that uses these references to construct residual representations that complement the original embeddings. Specifically, each memory derives a reference direction from its neighbors, and each query obtains its reference from a precomputed table. Using these references, NEAR constructs projection residuals for both queries and memories. These residuals are combined with the original embeddings for a single approximate nearest-neighbor search over a fixed memory index. Experiments on eight long-context retrieval benchmarks show consistent improvements across nine embedding models. Downstream evaluations show that NEAR improves question-answering performance.

Information Retrieval.title: Differentiable Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Predicting Cellular Responses to Gene Perturbation
Information Retrieval.summary: Predicting transcriptional responses to genetic perturbations is fundamental to functional genomics and therapeutic discovery. Recent deep learning models have shown promise in single-cell perturbation response prediction, but they typically generate each response in isolation, without explicitly leveraging related perturbations. We introduce PT-RAG (Perturbation-aware Two-stage Retrieval-Augmented Generation), a plug-in retrieval-and-conditioning module for generative cellular perturbation response. PT-RAG augments an existing perturbation-response backbone with learned access to related perturbation contexts. The key challenge is that relevance is not fixed in this setting: functionally related genes may elicit different effects across cell types. PT-RAG addresses this with a two-stage retrieval mechanism: GenePT-based semantic retrieval first identifies K candidate perturbations, after which a differentiable Gumbel-Softmax selector adaptively selects retrieved contexts conditioned on the control cell state, the query perturbation, and each candidate perturbation. We evaluate PT-RAG on two backbones, a STATE-style generator used as a frozen random reservoir and a fully trained scGPT, across cross-cell-type and cross-perturbation generalization tasks. PT-RAG consistently improves distributional similarity and often overall predictive quality; for example, on scGPT cross-cell-type results, the 2-Wasserstein distance drops by 5.9% relative to scGPT alone. The code to reproduce our experiments is available at https://github.com/difra100/PT-RAG_NIPS.
Information Retrieval.comment: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026 main track. 34 pages, 11 figures, 18 tables

Information Retrieval.title: PRIME: Pre-Retrieval Index Modeling Enhancement for Structured Document Retrieval-Real
Information Retrieval.summary: High-precision retrieval over external knowledge bases is essential for LLM agents to operate effectively. However, existing Information Retrieval (IR) research primarily optimizes query-side retrievers (e.g., ColBERT, BGE) and generators (e.g., Self-RAG, GraphRAG), while reducing corpus-side representation to chunking. This leaves index-side quality an underexplored lever. We propose Pre-Retrieval Index Modeling & Enhancement (PRIME), an index-side optimization framework built on two complementary tracks: an LLM-driven Semantic Restructuring (SR) track that transforms long documents into structured, information-dense sections, and a deterministic Metadata Synthesis (MS) and Hierarchical Retrieval (HR) track that extracts semantic anchors and heading structure for coarse-to-fine section retrieval. Our evaluations show that deterministic metadata matches structure-aware chunking's retrieval quality while cutting embedding computation by 45.8 $\times$ and index vector count by 22.4 $\times$. On top of these gains, Semantic Restructuring (SR) further improves Answer-F1 by 13.7% in full deployment, with characterized quality-fidelity-cost trade-offs. Across QASPER, BRIGHT, and NFCorpus, we further characterize three qualitative regimes that determine whether index-side optimization helps or degrades retrieval, while showing that these index-side effects are neutralized under a strong reranker.
Information Retrieval.comment: 9 pages, 2 figures. Manuscript completed July 2026. Supplementary material will be added in a future version

Information Retrieval.title: Beyond the Final Embedding: Retrieving Memories from Token-Level Evidence
Information Retrieval.summary: Memory-augmented assistants retrieve evidence from stored conversations and documents to answer queries. Most embedding-based retrievers compare single-vector representations of queries and memories, even when relevance depends on a small part of the content. Such local evidence can be matched to queries using the contextual token representations already computed by the same embedding models. Our method uses sparse token matching to improve retrieval without additional training. Each query token retrieves a small set of matching tokens across candidate memories. The matching scores are aggregated for each memory and combined with whole-memory similarity to rank memories. An optional low-rank query adapter can be trained with supervision while keeping the encoder and stored memory representations fixed. Our method improves retrieval across eight benchmarks and multiple model families without additional training. Query adaptation further increases the gains to 13.3 and 14.3 percentage points in average Recall@10 and NDCG@10 on Qwen3-Embedding-4B. These retrieval gains translate into higher question-answering accuracy on long-term memory benchmarks.

Information Retrieval.title: CRM: Retrieval Model with Controllable Condition
Information Retrieval.summary: Retrieval models for recommendation need to account for outcomes such as watch time while searching large item corpora efficiently. We present the Controllable Retrieval Model (CRM), an outcome-conditioned retrieval framework that adds watch time as an input to the user tower. During training, CRM learns to predict the next item given its observed watch time; at inference, we supply a desired watch time to steer retrieval without retraining. The item tower is independent of the condition, so item embeddings can still be precomputed and indexed for approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search. We implement CRM as both a DNN-based two-tower model and a Decision Transformer. The Transformer interleaves item tokens with watch-time-to-go condition tokens, using the target watch time as a numerical prompt for next-item prediction. For each online request, we choose between the average and maximum watch times in the user's recent history as the condition. CRM is deployed in Kuaishou's short-video recommendation system, which serves over 400 million users. Online A/B tests show video watch time improvements of 0.372% in Kuaishou and 0.457% in Kuaishou Lite.
Information Retrieval.comment: 4 pages. Revised version with improved presentation

Information Retrieval.title: UxSID: Semantic-Aware User Interests Modeling for Ultra-Long Sequence
Information Retrieval.summary: Modeling ultra-long user sequences involves a difficult trade-off between efficiency and effectiveness. While current paradigms rely on either item-specific search or item-agnostic compression, we propose UxSID, a framework exploring a third path: semantic-group shared interest memory. By utilizing Semantic IDs (SIDs) and a dual-level attention strategy, UxSID captures target-aware preferences without the heavy cost of item-specific models. This end-to-end architecture balances computational parsimony with semantic awareness, achieving state-of-the-art performance and a 0.337% revenue lift in large-scale advertising A/B test.

Information Retrieval.title: Locate, Judge, Read: Role-Specialized Tool Agents over a Knowledge-Point Index for Open-Domain Multimodal Document QA
Information Retrieval.summary: Question answering over large heterogeneous document collections requires first finding the right passages and then reading them, yet current retrieval-augmented agents give one model both kinds of tools and let it schedule itself. We present KnowForge, a pipeline separated by job: a hybrid-retrieval knowledge-point index; a Locator agent that can only search; a code-scheduled bridge judge that forces the missing second hop; a typed, size-bounded evidence pool that merges every search's ranking; a Deep Reader agent that can only read text, images and tables; and a synthesizer with a format checker. With a self-hosted Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (3B active), KnowForge reaches F1 47.5 on the full open-domain M3DocVQA (2,441 questions, 3,368 PDFs), +11.0 over the published M3DocRAG system and +7.1 over one-shot retrieve-and-answer on the same index and model, and 53.5 with DeepSeek-V4-Flash. On MultiHop-RAG it reaches 73.5 accuracy, above the strongest published RAG and GraphRAG results (71.2); on the single-document MMLongBench-Doc it lifts the same model from 34.8 to 47.0, level with GPT-4o reading page images (46.3). Per-job ablations on the full benchmarks attribute the gain: the Deep Reader is worth 3.8, 9.8 and 0 points on the three corpora, tracking how visual each is; merging both agents into one with all tools and twice the rounds loses 1.9 F1 because it keeps searching instead of reading; a round-budget sweep shows a step at four Locator rounds and a plateau beyond; query latency scales with model calls rather than corpus size. We serve the three indexed benchmarks as read-only knowledge bases (free registration) and release all prompts and the runner code: https://github.com/metask-ai/knowforge-bench
Information Retrieval.comment: 17 pages, 3 figures, 11 tables. Code, prompts and benchmark runner: https://github.com/metask-ai/knowforge-bench

Information Retrieval.title: Claim-Gated Source-Risk Auditing for Generative Search
Information Retrieval.summary: A generative search answer can cite a supported passage yet omit a source relationship that changes its interpretation. We specify a claim-gated audit of the query-source-answer tuple. An omission is resolved only when relationship evidence, answer adoption, materiality, and disclosure are all observed; incomplete evidence remains unresolved rather than being treated as independence. The specification separates this endpoint from citation support and review priority, and binds decisions to versioned evidence spans. A reference checker makes the record contract executable. On an exhaustive synthetic suite, it reproduces all 81 three-state predicate combinations and rejects 192 deliberately malformed records. Common-guard baselines and predicate ablations isolate endpoint logic from missing-evidence handling, while controlled transitions check support separation and evidence removal. These are finite contract-conformance results, not detector accuracy or evidence of improved user outcomes. We define the independent annotation, held-out evaluation, and paired utility tests still required to establish semantic validity and deployment benefit.
Information Retrieval.comment: 7 pages, 2 figures, 4 tables. Accepted at IEEE AI2A 2026. Author accepted manuscript. Reproducibility artifact: https://zenodo.org/records/23180013

Information Retrieval.title: Trust, but Validate the Instrument: Auditing AI-Generated RTL Verification Plans on Authored Security-Regression Proxies
Information Retrieval.summary: AI-generated RTL verification plans can satisfy a provider schema yet fail at the boundary to trusted execution. We present SecTB-RTL, an auditable framework covering 31 tasks and 124 authored hardware-security regressions. A deterministic non-AI baseline killed 36, 75, and 78 mutants at increasing resource limits. The first confirmatory run (C1-R2) failed before model execution because the provider rejected its response schema. After a schema-only repair made without viewing outcomes, a separately frozen follow-up run (C1-R3) completed 1,860 calls. The provider accepted 1,857 responses, but only nine passed the production semantic validator. The generation and execution rules did not match. We therefore preserve the run as an instrument-validation incident and report no prompt-effect estimate. This incident shows that provider or schema acceptance does not establish execution validity. Compilation and coverage are only diagnostics; the exact saved artifact must pass the full production path. A subsequent follow-up is excluded because it did not satisfy the preregistered evidence-completeness gate and is treated only as future work. We release the benchmark, failure-preserving contract, incident provenance, and governance controls needed to prevent infrastructure behavior from being misreported as model behavior.
Information Retrieval.comment: 7 pages, 3 table. Accepted at IEEE Cyber-AI 2026. Author accepted manuscript. Reproducibility artifact: https://zenodo.org/records/23230656

Information Retrieval.title: Imagine Before Acting: Prospective Skill Identification for LLM Agents
Information Retrieval.summary: Effective skill identification is crucial for LLM agents to reuse task-solving experience for complex task execution, which however remains challenging as agents must accurately identify useful skills from a large skill gallery and invoke them on demand. Existing studies have explored various strategies for skill retrieval and invocation, but largely overlook the natural discrepancy between task descriptions and skill documents. To be specific, our empirical study reveals that task descriptions mainly specify task objectives, whereas skill documents describe the required capabilities and procedural guidance for achieving the objectives. Such a so-called Task--Skill Misalignment (TSM) problem would cause desirable skills to be neglected during retrieval or remain unselected during invocation, thus hindering task execution. As a remedy, inspired by human prospective cognition, we propose SkillDreamer, a prospective skill identification framework to mitigate TSM. In brief, SkillDreamer first infers execution-required capabilities and imagines their realizations as pseudo skills, thereby translating task objectives into execution-oriented guidance for skill retrieval. As execution proceeds, SkillDreamer reevaluates the capabilities required by emerging subtasks to determine which skills should be invoked, thereby aligning skill invocation with evolving execution needs. Extensive experiments on three representative agent skill benchmarks not only verify the effectiveness of SkillDreamer in mitigating TSM, but also demonstrate its generalizability across diverse retrievers and LLM agents. The code will be released upon acceptance.
Information Retrieval.comment: 26 pages, including supplementary material. Substantially revised and extended version: expanded from skill retrieval to skill identification covering both retrieval and invocation, with additional experiments and analyses

Information Retrieval.title: Understanding and Mitigating Training Instability in Large-Scale Recommender Systems: A Cascade Perspective
Information Retrieval.summary: Training large-scale recommender systems on dynamic industrial platforms, such as Short-Form Video (SFV) services with billions of daily interactions, faces critical stability challenges. Rapid distribution shifts in user data and increasing model complexity frequently trigger a divergence cascade, typically initiating with gradient explosion, propagating to weight explosion, and culminating in loss explosion. This G-W-L cascade severely impedes model convergence and performance. This paper provides a systematic analysis of this G-W-L cascade within an industrial SFV recommender context. We then propose and evaluate a structured mitigation framework where interventions are explicitly mapped to counteract specific stages of the cascade: gradient (G) control, weight/activation (W) stabilization, and loss (L) shaping. Our contribution provides a structured framework for understanding and tackling training divergence, offering practical insights for deploying robust, continuously updated recommenders in large-scale, non-stationary settings. We empirically validate the effectiveness of these strategies on a major industrial SFV recommendation system.

Information Retrieval.title: Simple Linear Corrections for Compression in Late Interaction
Information Retrieval.summary:
Late-interaction (multi-vector) models represent documents using a set of token-level vectors, providing a middle ground between cross-encoders and dense encoders in terms of quality and cost of embedding. However, compared to the latter, the indices are costly to store and score. Pooling and pruning based compression techniques are deployed widely but deteriorate in quality noticeably with aggressive compression. We investigate whether a lightweight change to the scoring function can recover retrieval quality after document-vector compression. For each combination of encoder, compressor, and vector budget, we learn a global linear correction by distilling the uncompressed model's score distributions over candidate documents. The encoder and compressor remain frozen, and the correction can be applied to each query at search time or once, offline, to the stored vectors.
  We evaluate the method with ColBERTv2 and Jina v4 on MS MARCO and BEIR, and with ColPali2 on the ViDoRe v3 visual document retrieval benchmark. Experiments cover four training-free compression methods, multiple vector budgets, in-domain adaptation, and transfer from MS MARCO to BEIR. In the in-domain setting, the correction improves over baseline compression in 154 of 160 BEIR settings, while transfer from MS MARCO is more variable across models and datasets. We also find that matrices trained with synthetic queries can improve over baseline compression on ViDoRe v3. These results show that a small learned correction can recover some of the quality lost to compression without retraining the encoder or recompressing the documents.

Information Retrieval.title: Do you "see" what I "see"? A Multi-panel Visual Question Answer Dataset for Large Language Model Chart Analysis
Information Retrieval.summary: Digital libraries increasingly host scientific publications whose figures encode primary research findings, yet making this visual content searchable, accessible, and reusable remains an open challenge. Large language and multimodal models (LLMs/LMMs) provide the possibility to automate many figure parsing tasks such as determining data trends or extracting data from plots. In this work, we consider if these models can reliably support task-oriented visual data analysis when presented with synthetic, but realistic, scientific figures that contain multiple charts. Our Visual Question Answering (VQA) process scaffolds our tasks along a four-level description model from basic conceptual answers to interpretive and analytical understanding. Additionally, we outline our process for synthetically generating our single and multi-panel (charts in which there are multiple panels present) plots and testing the data with various LMMs using quantitative analysis. In general, we find LMMs become less accurate with increasing figure complexity as the number of panels, number of plot elements, and difficulty of questions increase. Finally, because LMM accuracy is expected to change rapidly, our analysis also considers cost relative to performance as a metric to inform future user decisions. We provide the detailed question-answer pairs used in this analysis, along with the code used to generate random plots, question-answer pairs and detailed bounding-box metadata for chart elements. The code and data are available at https://github.com/ReadingTimeMachine/LLM_VQA_MultiPanel and https://huggingface.co/datasets/ReadingTimeMachine/visual\_qa\_multipanel
Information Retrieval.comment: 16 pages, 4 figures, accepted to The 30th International Conference on Theory and Practice of Digital Libraries, 2026

Multimedia.title: DIA: A Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Interest-Aware ABR Scheme for Cloud Gaming
Multimedia.summary: The continuous evolution of cloud gaming has enabled users to play high-quality cloud games on thin clients, such as smartphones and tablets. However, how to effectively transmit the gameplay frames with high resolution and low latency, especially over wireless networks, remains a significant challenge. To address this challenge, we propose a Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL)-based Interest-Aware Adaptive Bitrate (ABR) scheme, called DIA, that guarantees the quality of perceptually key objects in each frame, while dynamically allocating lower resolutions for non-key objects to conserve bandwidth under constrained network conditions. By leveraging an off-the-shelf semantic segmentation model, the proposed DIA scheme can adjust the bitrate at the object-level. We also design a transformer-based feature extractor and an interest-aware reward function to enable the proposed DIA scheme to identify key objects and dynamically adjust their bitrates. This adaptation is guided by users' in-game movement speed, object features, and prevailing network conditions and operates without requiring additional hardware, such as gaze trackers. Extensive experiments show that the proposed DIA scheme outperforms existing ABR schemes in dynamic wireless network environments. Notably, DIA achieves at least a 20% higher normalized average Quality of Experience (QoE) than the State-Of-The-Art (SOTA) ABR algorithms in 5G scenarios.

Multimedia.title: EmoGavel: Grounding-Aware Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards for Multimodal Emotion Preference Learning
Multimedia.summary: Multimodal emotion preference learning uses pairwise comparisons to identify which open-ended emotion descriptions align more closely with human judgments. However, existing methods primarily focus on the final preference decision and provide little explicit supervision for localizing and correcting erroneous content. To address this limitation, we propose EmoGavel, a Grounding-Aware reinforcement learning framework with Verifiable rewards for multimodal Emotion preference Learning. We first introduce grounded supervised fine-tuning (Grounded SFT), which exploits controlled-error construction information to jointly learn preference prediction, error localization, repair, and missing-evidence recovery. We then optimize these verifiable outcomes with grounding-aware group relative policy optimization (GA-GRPO), combining preference-gated grounding rewards with dynamic zero-variance rescue to prioritize preference correctness and recover learning signals from all-wrong groups. Experiments on EmoPrefer and controlled-error evaluation sets show that EmoGavel improves both natural preference prediction and controlled-error discrimination while maintaining strong error-grounding performance. Our code and model checkpoints will be released once the paper is accepted.

Multimedia.title: CV-OPD: Contrastive Vision On-policy Distillation
Multimedia.summary: On-policy distillation (OPD) reveals versatility and convenience during VLM post-training, providing dense supervision for student from teacher. However, we observed an anomaly that the distilled VLM could still answer the questions accurately even when the related visual regions were masked or replaced with noise. Building on this observation, our quantitative and qualitative experiments demonstrate that OPD, which uses the answer as a hint, has failed to teach students to genuinely seek out and rely on visual evidence. Our theoretical analysis suggests that this failure arises from a shortcut enabled by the lack of visual constraints during distillation. To address the issue, we introduce Contrastive Vision On-policy Distillation (CV-OPD), which compares teacher distributions induced by positive and negative crops while conditioning on the same student prefix and augments optimization with a margin-based contrastive constraint, which is modulated with discrepancy gating across token and sample level. Specifically, CV-OPD first introduces a negative teacher unrelated to the answer and designs a Contrastive Divergence Loss (CDL) that constrains the feature distribution of student by contrasting the positive and negative teachers, correcting how the student exploits visual regions. The CV-OPD introduces a Discrepancy Aware Gate (DAG) that uses token-level and sample-level discrepancies to select visually relevant tokens for optimization, directing the student's attention toward visual content. Extensive experiments across a broad range of fine-grained visual benchmarks demonstrate that CV-OPD substantially alleviates shortcut and consistently improves the visual reasoning capabilities of existing VLMs.
Multimedia.comment: 16 pages, 7 figures, contrastive learning for on-policy distillation of VLMs. Computer Vision. Post-training. VLM. LLM

Multimedia.title: MotionCoach: Constructing Multimodal Guidance for Video Professional Motion Editing
Multimedia.summary: Video editing models achieve strong performance in modifying appearance, backgrounds, styles, and motions, empowered by large-scale training data. Beyond general scenarios, professional motions are significant in performance, sports, and martial arts. This paper focuses on professional motion editing, which involves fine-grained motion technique and temporal structure. Given professional motion names but lacking detailed descriptions, existing models often fail to generate professional motions, such as incorrectly lifting the front wheel under a Stoppie instruction. To address this challenge, we introduce MotionCoach, a trained multimodal agent that uses multi-turn tools and performs self-verification, producing a grounded prompt and a reference clip as reliable and sufficient multimodal guidance to inject external professional motion knowledge into video editing models. To supply training data, we build a data pipeline to construct trajectories. We cold-start the agent on MotionCoach-SFT-10k and apply Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) on MotionCoach-RL-2k with rewards on the motion guidance prompt, the motion outcome video, and the format. For evaluation, we introduce VPMEBench, comprising 314 professional motion editing tasks with fine-grained references and annotations. Extensive experiments show that MotionCoach improves the overall score from 55.1 to 65.6 on Seedance 2.0 and from 51.2 to 64.5 on MiniMax-H3. Learning to construct multimodal guidance enables precise professional motion editing without retraining video editing models.

Image and Video Processing.title: A Miniaturized Wi-Fi HaLow-Based Wireless Imaging Transfer System for Capsule Endoscopy
Image and Video Processing.summary:
Wireless capsule endoscopy is constrained by severe limitations in size, available power, and reliable data transmission through biological tissues. Although recent advances in miniature imaging sensors have improved image quality, the wireless transmission of color images at practical frame rates remains a challenging task under the tight capsule constraints.
  We present the design and the experimental validation of a miniaturized Wireless Imaging Transfer (WIT) system for capsule endoscopy based on a sub-GHz IEEE 802.11ah (Wi-Fi HaLow) wireless link. In addition, a preliminary in-vivo validation of Wi-Fi HaLow communication is reported, showing that a stable through-body wireless link can be established across biological tissues in a clinically relevant porcine model. These in-vivo results provide direct experimental support for the adoption of sub-GHz Wi-Fi HaLow for capsule endoscopy applications.
  Experimental results demonstrate stable wireless image transmission at a resolution of 320x320 pixels, with measured end-to-end data rates above 12 Mbps and a transmission energy efficiency of 20.7 nJ/bit. We also report a detailed power consumption analysis, with a breakdown of the contributions from the imaging sensor, illumination, digital processing, and RF transmission. When all active subsystem contributions are considered, including the camera, digital processing, RF transmission, and illumination at 60% LED brightness, the total power consumption is approximately 477 mW, corresponding to a complete-chain energy consumption of approximately 39.6 nJ/bit. Overall, the measured performance confirms that sub-GHz Wi-Fi HaLow provides a promising trade-off among throughput, robustness, and energy efficiency for wireless imaging in capsule endoscopy.

Image and Video Processing.title: Can Multimodal Decision Models Classify Breast Ultrasound Images? Benchmarking CLEF and CLEF-Flash Across Prompts and Datasets
Image and Video Processing.summary: Multimodal decision models return probabilities over predefined alternatives, offering a structured interface for image classification. This study benchmarks inference with CLEF and CLEF-Flash on 2818 breast ultrasound images from Dataset B, BUSI, and BUS-BRA. Dataset B and BUS-BRA use binary benign-malignant classification, whereas BUSI includes normal, benign, and malignant categories. Model parameters remain unchanged, and original images are submitted without user-defined preprocessing. Three prompts provide minimal labels, an explicit classification task, or sonographic criteria. We report accuracy, macro F1, balanced accuracy, macro precision, throughput, and latency. CLEF-Flash with the clinical prompt achieves the highest accuracy on all three datasets: 74.85% on Dataset B, 66.28% on BUSI, and 51.63% on BUS-BRA. On BUSI, however, CLEF with the task-guided prompt achieves the highest macro F1 (64.51%) and balanced accuracy (68.72%). CLEF-Flash has lower latency in every matched comparison. Clinical instructions improve CLEF-Flash accuracy relative to the minimal prompt but reduce CLEF accuracy on all datasets. Confusion matrices reveal frequent benign-to-malignant errors, particularly on BUS-BRA, where all configurations fall below the 67.63% accuracy of a majority-class predictor. These findings demonstrate dataset-and prompt-dependent performance and motivate class-specific evaluation before applying multimodal decision models to breast ultrasound analysis.

Image and Video Processing.title: Model-agnostic Knowledge Augmented Machine Learning for Weakly Annotated Bioimaging Data
Image and Video Processing.summary: Machine learning models are increasingly used for automated feature extraction from weakly annotated bioimaging data, such as microscopy and cytomorphology images. Due to the sole dependency of automated feature extraction, existing methods yield inconsistent classification performance across weakly annotated datasets. Here, we propose a model-agnostic knowledge augmentation method that enables ML models to exploit domain knowledge beyond what automated feature extraction can capture. The proposed approach improves classification performance across seven ML architectures. When integrated with masked autoencoder-based self-supervised learning, our method achieves the strongest overall performance, improving precision by 2.9% over the next-best method on three in-house microscopy datasets and by an average of 6.8% across three public cytomorphology benchmarks. We perform nucleus-level classification based on mislocalization of TAR DNA-binding protein 43 (TDP-43) from the nucleus to the cytoplasm, a phenotype linked to Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS), using three independent microscopy datasets of motor neurons derived from human induced pluripotent stem cells. Accurate quantification of this phenotype at scale remains challenging and may contribute to inconsistencies across studies. Application of the best-performing model to these microscopy datasets reveals biological interpretations related to ALS, including dose-dependent effects of the proteasomal stressor, MG132, and the oxidative stressor, sodium arsenite (SA), on TDP-43 mislocalization, variable pathology in motor neurons from sporadic and familial ALS donors, and a lack of protection of the pharmacological compounds, edaravone and niclosamide, against SA-induced TDP-43 mislocalization. Together, our pipeline enables in-vitro cellular image analysis to advance understanding of ALS-associated pathology and potential treatments.

Image and Video Processing.title: Desertification Forecasting in Semi-Arid Regions: Using Deep Learning to Probe the Observability Limits of Land Degradation Dynamics
Image and Video Processing.summary: Forecasting desertification has received far less attention than mapping it. We use a convolutional LSTM (ConvLSTM) trained on ten annual Earth Observation (EO) variables (2000-2023) over the semi-arid state of Ceará, Brazil, on a 256x206 grid at roughly 2.2 km resolution, to measure how much of the year-to-year evolution of a MapBiomas-derived degradation index (IDV) can be predicted from satellite data. The network predicts a bounded change on top of the last observed state, is trained in two stages (single-step, then recursive rollout) and is evaluated on a contiguous spatial and temporal holdout. State-wide mean IDV rose from 0.238 to 0.350 between 2000 and 2023, about 0.005 per year, but cell-level change is dominated by year-to-year jumps, and a gradient-boosting model given all channels explains only 4.7% of its variance. Against this ceiling, the ConvLSTM lowers RMSE relative to persistence by 1.6% one year ahead and 4.4% four years ahead in a held-out southern band (p < 0.001), beats persistence with a constant drift and reproduces 53-69% of the regional drift. Drift-aware baselines only help from the third year onward, by up to 4.4% in RMSE at six years. An earlier formulation that redrew the whole field each year predicted changes unrelated to the observed ones (correlation -0.06) and produced a spurious decline when run recursively. Channel knockouts suggest that elevation and EVI degrade the forecast, while slope and aspect have no measurable effect. Monte Carlo dropout and stochastic scenario maps convey the uncertainty that the expected-value forecast hides. Under climatological forcing, mean IDV rises from 0.350 in 2023 to 0.370 in 2030. EO-based desertification forecasting is therefore reliable for the regional trend, not for individual cells.
Image and Video Processing.comment: 14 pages, 10 figures, 7 tables

Image and Video Processing.title: Radiomics-Based Thyroid Nodule Classification with Label-Conditional Conformal Prediction
Image and Video Processing.summary: Thyroid nodule malignancy assessment relies on ultrasound imaging, yet current risk stratification systems suffer from substantial interobserver variability, contributing to a high rate of unnecessary biopsies. We propose a radiomics-based framework combining quantitative feature extraction via PyRadiomics with a Generalized Additive Model (GAM) classifier, selected among six candidates for its favorable trade-off between discriminative performance and interpretability. To complement point predictions with uncertainty estimates, Cross-Conformal Prediction with label-conditional guarantees is applied, flagging ambiguous cases for clinical review rather than forcing a binary decision. Experiments are conducted on TN5000, a publicly available ultrasound dataset of thyroid nodules. After Spearman correlation filtering, 36 features are retained and the GAM achieves an AUC of $0.89$, a sensitivity of $0.83$, and a specificity of $0.82$ on the validation set. At a significance level $ε=0.09$, selected to ensure empirical coverage guarantees on both classes, 63\% of nodules on the test set receive a certain (i.e., single-label) prediction, with conditional precision of $0.94$ for certain malignant and conditional Negative Predictive Value (NPV) of $0.73$ for certain benign cases, while the remaining 37\% are referred to the clinician.
Image and Video Processing.comment: Accepted at the CIBB 2026 conference (https://cibb2026.teralab.ai/)

Image and Video Processing.title: Leveraging Motion Estimation for Efficient Bayer-Domain Video Convolutional Networks
Image and Video Processing.summary: Existing computer vision pipelines suffer from two efficiency bottlenecks: image signal processors (ISPs) first convert Bayer pixel data to RGB pixel by pixel, and video models repeatedly process temporally redundant frames, leading to high power consumption and latency. In this paper, we propose a novel framework that eliminates the ISP and leverages motion estimation to accelerate video vision tasks directly in the Bayer domain. We introduce Motion Estimation-based Video Convolution (MEVC), which integrates sliding-window motion estimation into each convolutional layer, enabling prediction and residual-based refinement that reduces redundant computations across frames. This design bridges the structural gap between block-based motion estimation and spatial convolution, enabling accurate, low-cost processing. Our end-to-end pipeline supports raw Bayer input and achieves over 70% reduction in FLOPs with minimal accuracy degradation across video semantic segmentation, depth estimation, and object detection benchmarks, using both synthetic Bayer-converted and real Bayer video datasets.

Image and Video Processing.title: Selective Depthwise Separable Convolution for Lightweight Joint Source-Channel Coding in Wireless Image Transmission
Image and Video Processing.summary: Depthwise separable convolutional (DSConv) layers have been successfully applied to deep learning (DL)-based joint source-channel coding (JSCC) schemes to reduce computational complexity. However, a systematic investigation of the layerwise and ratio-wise replacement of standard convolutional (Conv) layers with DSConv layers in JSCC systems for wireless image transmission remains largely unexplored. In this letter, we propose a configurable lightweight JSCC framework that incorporates a selective replacement strategy, enabling flexible Conv-to-DSConv replacement at different replacement ratios and positions. By varying the replacement ratio, we obtain models with different computational complexities and analyze their impact on reconstruction performance. Furthermore, we investigate how replacements at different encoder and decoder depths influence reconstruction quality under a fixed replacement ratio. Our results show that Conv-to-DSConv replacement at the intermediate layers of the encoder and decoder achieves a favorable complexity-performance trade-off, revealing layer-wise redundancy in DL-based JSCC systems. Extensive experiments further demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves substantial parameter reduction with only slight performance degradation, enabling flexible complexity-performance trade-offs for resource-constrained edge devices.
Image and Video Processing.comment: 6 pages, 6 figures, journal

Image and Video Processing.title: The Predictability Bias of Joint-Embedding Predictive Learning in Medical Imaging
Image and Video Processing.summary: Joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs) learn by predicting teacher representations of masked regions from visible context. Point prediction summarizes the conditional target distribution and cannot reproduce variation that the context does not resolve. We call this constraint predictability bias. In computed tomography (CT), recurrent anatomy is predictable from context, whereas the sporadic, localized pathology that determines clinical interpretation often is not. We introduce TAP-JEPA, a ViT-B/3D trained on 113,611 CT volumes that is competitive with state-of-the-art encoders (COLIPRI, Merlin, VoxelFM) in scan-level classification. We then audit the learned predictive pathway by replaying the exact masking, teacher, and predictor computations used during training. Prediction lowers the mean Skill (prevalence-normalized average precision) from 0.388 to 0.271 for pathology, but only from 0.921 to 0.873 for anatomy. Along the teacher direction, separating pathology from matched control regions in the same organ, prediction moves pathology 34.7% toward the controls and controls 13.6% toward pathology, with larger shifts farther from visible context. Replacing visible matched-control representations increases surrounding-target prediction loss more than fully replacing pathology representations across four pathology categories. Downstream, removing all final-layer pathology tokens reduces the decision margin by at most 0.45% in four of seven scan-level probes. Together, these results show that contextual predictability is not a sufficient proxy for clinical relevance in medical representation learning. Training objectives should therefore retain diagnostic features regardless of their predictability from surrounding anatomy.
Image and Video Processing.comment: 45 pages, 6 figures

Image and Video Processing.title: Stochastic Finite-Transition Learning and Exploration for Accelerated MRI Reconstruction
Image and Video Processing.summary: Generative MRI reconstruction maps an initial source distribution to the target image distribution along a learned recovery trajectory. Common generative methods, such as diffusion and flow, typically learn fine-grained local dynamics whose integration defines this global mapping, hence requiring many network evaluations at inference. Existing few-step sampling approaches can lower computational burden by approximating large transformations from local dynamics, albeit at the expense of reconstruction fidelity. FLEX-MRI instead partitions recovery into a small number of finite intervals between retained states defined by progressive changes in k-space support, and directly learns the reconstruction change across each interval. Because such finite transitions can admit multiple plausible outcomes, FLEX-MRI combines support-relaxed finite-transition learning with stochastic exploration. During training, randomized k-space sampling masks define finite-transition targets with varying support, while the prediction loss remains unrestricted by each individual mask. At inference, FLEX-MRI perturbs a random subset of currently estimated k-space coefficients, allowing the learned predictor to stochastically explore alternative transition paths. Each predicted state is then reconciled with the acquired measurements through data consistency. We theoretically show that this stochastic exploration induces nonzero transition-level variation through the learned recovery map and data consistency without requiring an auxiliary generative sampler. Experiments on multi-coil MRI datasets show that FLEX-MRI outperforms competing methods while maintaining computational efficiency comparable to few-step baselines.

Image and Video Processing.title: One-Bin Fourier Challenges for Dimension-Free Reconstruction Certification
Image and Video Processing.summary: Partial-Fourier measurement underlies computational imaging, and its reconstructions increasingly come from iterative or learned solvers whose recovery guarantees are conditional on a signal model, a sampling law, and solver accuracy. None of those guarantees transfers to a particular committed output: it can satisfy every acquired coefficient while remaining badly wrong in the unmeasured nullspace. Native Fourier holdout does not repair this, since a spectrally concentrated error is missed unless its bin is drawn, so uniform worst-case risk needs a number of hidden bins proportional to the dimension. We propose a post-commit acceptance test: secret finite-phase masks turn one fixed Fourier readout into dense randomized residual checks, and a median-of-means threshold handles calibrated readout noise. We prove that errors above $E_{\rm rej}$ are rejected and errors below $E_{\rm acc}$ are accepted with confidence $1-δ$ once $q\ge C(1+Nσ^2/E_{\rm rej})^2\log(1/δ)$, explicitly exposing the one-bin resolution floor $Nσ^2/\sqrt q$; in the zero-noise limit, QPSK gives $4^{-q}$ soundness versus $97.9\%$ minimax false acceptance for a worst-case ordinary-bin error. At a fixed noise-to-threshold ratio, measured screening false acceptance fell from about $21\%$ at 16 checks to $5\%$ at 64; a data-consistent learned nullspace failure with NMSE $0.200$ was rejected by $96.9\%$ of challenge banks while 16 ordinary bins missed it $98.9\%$ of the time; and error statistics at 16 checks stayed stable from 128 through $65{,}536$ dimensions. The test supports solver acceptance, model selection, and stopping certification, with a certified fresh-bank error interval.
Image and Video Processing.comment: The author withdraws this paper because the coded-diffraction implementation claimed in Section 3.3 is not established. The certification procedure requires complex-valued linear Fourier measurements, whereas intensity-only acquisition does not directly provide them. The manuscript does not establish the additional acquisition procedure needed to bridge this gap

Image and Video Processing.title: Low, High, and Semantic-Level Vision-Language Learning for AI-Generated Image Detection
Image and Video Processing.summary: Driven by advances in diffusion models and autoregressive models, the fidelity and resolution of AI-generated images now rival those of real images. However, existing AI-generated image detection methods often downsample the images,inevitably overlooking critical low-level texture details in high-resolution AI-generated images, thereby limiting their detection performance. In addition, the continuous emergence of unknown generative models makes large-scale pre-training datasets inaccessible. To address these challenges, we propose a novel AI-generated image detector, termed LHSDet (Low-, High-, and Semantic-level Detection). Specifically, we formulate the AI-generated image detection task as a Visual Question Answering problem, leveraging a fine-tuned vision-language framework to fully exploit the complementary information between visual and textual modalities. Recognizing that the default visual encoder of existing vision-language models is not tailored for AI-generated image detection, we redesign a visual encoder to better capture both the low-level and high-level artifacts inherent in AI-generated images. Furthermore, we incorporate a semantic-level textual branch to enable multi-modal feature fusion and detection. Consequently, LHSDet employs a triple-branch architecture to extract complementary multi-modal features: a low-level visual branch that aggregates non-overlapping patches for local texture cues, a high-level visual branch based on SigLIP2 for global perception feature extraction,and a semantic-level textual branch that generates captions using BLIP-2. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that LHSDet achieves strong detection accuracy and robust performance across diverse generative models.

Image and Video Processing.title: Compression Hurts, Pooling Helps: Information Loss in Rayleigh-Scale Estimation from B-Mode Ultrasound
Image and Video Processing.summary: Clinical B-mode images are widely available as potential data sources for quantitative ultrasound (QUS) analysis for tissue characterization. However, standard clinical ultrasound devices apply unknown log-compression to RF envelope data before display and storage. Previous work has demonstrated estimation of the underlying RF envelope statistics in the presence of an unknown compression law. Using Fisher information analysis, we show that finite-offset log compression causes severe information loss when estimating the Rayleigh scale $σ$, which controls diffuse speckle. For a single image window, unknown compression raises the minimum achievable variance for unbiased estimation of $σ$ by a compression-independent factor of approximately 34.98. When $M$ equal-sized windows share the same unknown compression settings, the excess variance decays as $1/M$; even in the most favorable regime, reducing the variance inflation factor below 1.1 requires 340 windows. Our analysis treats the contrast parameter $a$ as unknown and the boundary offset $b$ as known; estimating $b$ experimentally shows even larger variance. We validate this theory using synthetic estimation experiments and demonstrate RF-scale recovery on real RF-envelope windows from the OASBUD dataset. Together, these results clarify the limitations of using routine B-mode images for QUS.
Image and Video Processing.comment: 20 pages, 7 figures

Image and Video Processing.title: Scale-specific auxiliary multi-task contrastive learning for deep liver vessel segmentation
Image and Video Processing.summary: Extracting hepatic vessels from abdominal images is of high interest for clinicians since it allows to divide the liver into functionally-independent Couinaud segments. In this respect, an automated liver blood vessel extraction is widely summoned. Despite the significant growth in performance of semantic segmentation methodologies, preserving the complex multi-scale geometry of main vessels and ramifications remains a major challenge. This paper provides a new deep supervised approach for vessel segmentation, with a strong focus on representations arising from the different scales inherent to the vascular tree geometry. In particular, we propose a new clustering technique to decompose the tree into various scale levels, from tiny to large vessels. Then, we extend standard 3D UNet to multi-task learning by incorporating scale-specific auxiliary tasks and contrastive learning to encourage the discrimination between scales in the shared representation. Promising results, depicted in several evaluation metrics, are revealed on the public 3D-IRCADb dataset.
Image and Video Processing.comment: 5 pages, 5 figures, IEEE ISBI 2023. v2: fixed a figure reference. Code for the multi-scale vessel clustering (Sect. 2.1): https://github.com/asadikine/vessel-scale-clustering

Image and Video Processing.title: Multiclass histogram-based thresholding using kernel density estimation and scale-space representations
Image and Video Processing.summary: We present a method for multiclass thresholding of histograms whose modes may overlap so strongly that they merge into a unimodal distribution. The histogram is approximated by a nonparametric kernel density (KD) estimate, a mixture of Gaussians with one component per bin and a common bandwidth, whose parameters are determined by Expectation-Maximization (EM) iterations. Because the estimate is a Gaussian mixture, the semigroup property of Gaussian convolution yields its scale-space representation in closed form, at bandwidths both larger and smaller than the fitted one. The algorithm increases or decreases the bandwidth until the number of local minima of the estimate equals the number of requested classes minus one, and returns the positions of those minima as the threshold values. We validate the method on synthetic histograms with known thresholds, and we apply it to the histogram of X-ray computed tomography images of a natural porous sample in which the three phases strongly overlap. The porosity computed from the resulting segmentation agrees with the direct experimental measurement to within 4%, whereas K-means clustering misestimates it by 52%.

Image and Video Processing.title: Beyond Gate Weights: Decision-Level Interpretation of Radiomics-Image Feature Fusion for RCC Classification
Image and Video Processing.summary: Gate coefficients describe how a fusion layer weights intermediate features, but they do not necessarily reflect the magnitude of branch contributions at the classifier output. We investigate this distinction in a fixed 3D MedVAE--radiomics model for clear cell versus non-clear cell renal cell carcinoma classification from contrast-enhanced CT. Because the model uses a linear classification head, the binary decision logit can be decomposed exactly into a gated image term, a direct radiomics term, and a bias. We define effective radiomics dominance as the direct radiomics term's share of the summed absolute non-bias branch contributions and compare it with structural radiomics weighting. Internally, mean structural radiomics weighting was 0.823, whereas mean effective radiomics dominance was 0.148, with a modest case-wise association (\r{ho} = 0.290). The gated image term retained substantially stronger discriminative ranking information than the direct radiomics term. The same structural-to-effective discrepancy was observed in exploratory external evaluation. Branch-targeted permutation, integrated-gradient, and Shapley-style analyses further identified radiomics descriptors influencing the direct radiomics term. Because radiomics also generates the gate, the gated image term remains radiomics-dependent, so additive branch contribution should not be interpreted as total input influence. These findings show that structural gate weighting and decision-level branch contribution represent distinct aspects of gated feature fusion and should be interpreted separately.
Image and Video Processing.comment: 12 pages, 1 figure. Accepted at the 2026 Irish Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Cognitive Science (AICS 2026). Proceedings forthcoming

Image and Video Processing.title: Beyond Discrimination: Evaluating Probability Calibration in Radiomics-Image Fusion for Renal Cell Carcinoma Classification
Image and Video Processing.summary: Reliable probability estimates are important for the clinical interpretation of machine-learning classifiers, yet radiomics--image fusion models for renal cell carcinoma (RCC) are commonly evaluated primarily by discrimination. Using 396 patients from the KiTS23 dataset, we evaluated whether adding radiomics to four image-model families improved probabilistic performance in addition to discrimination. Seventeen individual models and four probability-average ensembles were assessed using discrimination, probability calibration, and proper scoring measures. Across 12 matched image-only versus fusion comparisons, AUC and AP improved in all 12, while Brier score and negative log likelihood (NLL) improved in 11 of 12 and expected calibration error (ECE) in eight of 12. The 3D MedVAE gated-fusion model achieved the strongest overall individual-model profile. Probability averaging across concatenation, cross-attention, and gated fusion produced favourable point estimates across all five primary metrics relative to image-only models in all four families, although paired-bootstrap support was stronger for Brier score and NLL than for ECE. These findings show that radiomics--image fusion can improve probabilistic prediction quality beyond discrimination, while calibration behaviour varies across image architectures and fusion strategies. We show that our proposed probability-average ensemble models improve discrimination and calibration simultaneously across all architectures in the study.
Image and Video Processing.comment: 12 pages. 1 figure. Accepted at the 2026 Irish Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Cognitive Science (AICS 2026). Proceedings forthcoming

Image and Video Processing.title: C$^2$LUE: Clinically Aligned Patient-Level Ultrasound Diagnosis via Evidence-Aware Multi-Instance Learning
Image and Video Processing.summary: Patient-level ultrasound diagnosis demands not only high predictive accuracy but also clinically aligned mitigation of asymmetric diagnostic risks. While Multi-Instance Learning (MIL) effectively models routine multi-view exams, standard aggregators often dilute heterogeneous diagnostic cues and optimize solely for global accuracy. This frequently yields undesirable sensitivity-specificity trade-offs. To bridge this gap, we propose C$^2$LUE, a novel MIL framework coupling evidence aware aggregation with risk-aligned regularization. To preserve evidence heterogeneity and prevent unimodal attention collapse, C$^2$LUE employs a multi-query cross-attention mechanism built upon a LoRA-adapted DINOv3 backbone. Multiple latent queries explicitly extract and disentangle diverse morphological patterns from the ultrasound sequence. Furthermore, to improve clinical risk alignment, we introduce a dynamic trade-off regularization objective that penalizes sensitivity-specificity imbalance during training. Rather than leaving the clinical trade-off entirely to post-hoc threshold adjustment, this objective encourages the learned score distribution toward a more balanced operating region. Extensive evaluations on patient-level, biopsy-proven thyroid and breast ultrasound datasets demonstrate that C$^2$LUE consistently outperforms prior alternatives. By uniting strong discrimination with a balanced error profile, C$^2$LUE provides a promising solution for real-world ultrasound screening and diagnosis.

Image and Video Processing.title: Frozen Site-Probe Accuracy Is Not a Standalone Harmonization Score: An Audit of Evaluation Practice for Multi-Site MRI
Image and Video Processing.summary: Image-level MRI harmonization is often evaluated with a frozen site probe, a site classifier trained on raw scans and applied unchanged to harmonized ones: a drop in its accuracy is read as removal of site effects. We audit this practice on ABIDE I (1,112 T1-weighted scans, 17 sites) with ten output sets from seven harmonization methods and controls for chance, head shape, intensity, preprocessing and target alignment. We find that this verdict depends on how the probe is trained, even among probes that classify raw scans well: across random seeds, its balanced accuracy on the same CycleGAN outputs ranges from 0.13 to 0.59 (chance: 0.06). Low frozen-probe accuracy can also arise without harmonization: a Gaussian blur, which increases the intensity distance to the target site, lowers this accuracy to chance. Moreover, where the frozen probe fails, probes trained on the harmonized scans still recover the site, even from intensity histograms alone: on HACA3 outputs, the frozen probe scores 0.25, a probe trained on those outputs 0.75, and one using only their intensity histograms 0.71. Low frozen-probe accuracy therefore does not show that site information has been removed. We recommend reporting several probes trained to convergence, probes trained on harmonized scans, and target alignment.
Image and Video Processing.comment: 4 pages, 2 figures, 1 table. Submitted to IEEE ISBI 2027. Code and results: https://github.com/muqsitamir/HarmonIt. This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication. Copyright may be transferred without notice, after which this version may no longer be accessible

Image and Video Processing.title: Exploring the Latent Structure of AMD Severity Using Retinal Foundation Models
Image and Video Processing.summary: Retinal foundation models have demonstrated strong performance across a wide range of ophthalmic tasks, yet relatively little is known about how disease-related information is represented within their learned embeddings and whether this distribution influences downstream prediction performance. In this work, we use Age-related Macular Degeneration (AMD) as a case study to investigate how disease severity is represented within the embedding space of RET-CLIP, a retinal vision-language foundation model, using bilateral fundus images from the AREDS dataset, benchmarked against non-retinal encoders. We first characterize the distribution of AMD severity within the learned representation space and then evaluate how this structure influences classification performance across three clinically relevant task formulations of increasing granularity. Finally, we analyze the most influential latent dimensions combining feature attribution, statistical phenotype association, and qualitative image analyses. Our results show that RET-CLIP represents AMD severity as a continuous spectrum rather than a set of discrete categories, with healthy and advanced disease stages exhibiting clearer separation than intermediate ones. This organization was reflected in downstream performance, which decreased from a balanced accuracy of 0.844 and 0.814 for binary AMD and Late-AMD detection respectively to 0.446 for six-class grading. Furthermore, the most influential latent dimensions were statistically associated to distinct retinal phenotypes, including drusen accumulation, pigmentary alterations, and advanced retinal lesions. These findings suggest that the structure of retinal foundation-model representations influences the difficulty of clinically relevant prediction tasks and demonstrate the potential of representation-level analysis for understanding disease organization and improving interpretability.
Image and Video Processing.comment: 7 pages, 5 figures. Accepted for publication at IEEE EMBS BHI 2026

Systems and Control.title: Goal-Oriented Bundle Management and Flow Control for Deep-Space Communications via Reinforcement Learning
Systems and Control.summary: Deep-space communications operate under intermittent connectivity, long propagation delays, and relay storage constraints. In such networks, the Bundle Protocol enables store-carry-forward communication, requiring relay nodes to manage limited storage and scarce contact opportunities. Relay-side scheduling and dropping decisions are inherently goal-oriented: transmission resources should be allocated to bundles most valuable to downstream mission objectives. Conventional schedulers, such as FIFO, do not explicitly optimize task utility and may provide unfair service across heterogeneous planetary sources. This paper presents a closed-loop modeling and learning framework for relay-side bundle and flow management in a contact-driven deep-space network, where lunar and Martian updates are forwarded through a shared-buffer relay to Earth. We quantify destination-side information freshness using excess age $Δ_i^e(t)=[Δ_i(t)-d_i(t)]^+$, where $Δ_i(t)$ denotes the Age of Information of source $i$ and $d_i(t)$ is a source-dependent delay baseline. Based on this metric, we define a goal-oriented loss that supports source-dependent nonlinear penalties, allowing prioritization according to mission relevance.
