ACGP is embedded in a receding-horizon controller that evaluates five-step candidate futures, executes the selected intervention, and replans from the observed next state. The final dataset contains 2,860 counter factual roots and 22,880 action-conditioned branches. On the held-out test set, ACGP achieves a five-step line-loading MAE of 0.0369 and a redispatch pairwise ranking accuracy of 0.806; action ablations reduce the ranking accuracy to approximately chance level. In closed-loop Grid2Op experiments, terminal-failure and cascade rates decrease from 53.3% and 51.1% under do-nothing operation to 12.2% and 7.8%, respectively, close to the simulator-reference values of 11.1% and 6.7%. The results show that same-state counterfactual prediction can support effective action comparison and feedback-based cascading-failure mitigation.

Systems and Control.title: Tube-Based Robust Control Strategy for Vision-Guided Autonomous Vehicles
Systems and Control.summary: A robust control strategy for autonomous vehicles can improve system stability, enhance riding comfort, and prevent driving accidents. This paper presents a novel interpolation-tubebased constrained iterative linear quadratic regulator (itubeCILQR) algorithm for autonomous computer-vision-based vehicle lane-keeping. The goal of the algorithm is to enhance robustness during high-speed cornering on tight turns. Compared with standard tube-based approaches, the proposed itube-CILQR algorithm reduces system conservatism and exhibits higher computational speed. Numerical simulations and vision-based experiments were conducted to examine the feasibility of using the proposed algorithm for controlling autonomous vehicles. The results indicated that the proposed algorithm achieved superior vehicle lane-keeping performance to variational CILQRbased methods and model predictive control (MPC) approaches involving the use of a classical interior-point optimizer. Specifically, itube-CILQR required an average runtime of 3.45 ms to generate a control signal for guiding a self-driving vehicle. By comparison, itube-MPC typically required a 4.32 times longer computation time to complete the same task. Moreover, the influence of conservatism on system behavior was investigated by exploring the variations in the interpolation variables derived using the proposed itube-CILQR algorithm during lane-keeping maneuvers.
Systems and Control.comment: 15 pages, 11 figures

Systems and Control.title: Deploying RDMA for Distributed Inference and Training At Scale
Systems and Control.summary: RDMA can reduce communication overhead in distributed machine learning systems, but realizing these benefits in production requires more than replacing TCP. Variable-size messages, concurrent connections, bursty incasts, and service failures introduce challenges that hardware offload alone cannot address. This paper reports our experience deploying ByteExpress, a software communication layer over hardware RDMA, in ByteDance's parameter-server-based inference and training systems. We present three lessons from the deployment: efficient RDMA requires buffer management across application and transport layers; scalable communication requires coordinated management of connections, receive capacity, and outstanding data; and service availability requires recovery above the transport layer. ByteExpress combines an RDMA-aware allocator, zero-copy transfers, QP multiplexing, receive-credit flow control, a software send window, and RPC-assisted recovery. In production inference, ByteExpress reduces mean and P99 model parameter fetch latency by 35.7% and 43.7%, respectively, and total CPU usage by 10.69% compared with kernel TCP. In training, ByteExpress reduces P99 model parameter push latency by up to 74.0% compared with TCP, with no PFC pauses observed at runtime.
Systems and Control.comment: 14 pages, 16 figures

Systems and Control.title: Controller-Agnostic Runtime Safety Certificates for Tool-Using AI Agents via Data-Driven Robust Reachability
Systems and Control.summary: Software agents built on large language models act by issuing tool calls, some of which cannot be undone. To control theory the model is an opaque feedback controller, replaced every few months, whose closed loop cannot be analyzed directly. We propose a runtime filter, or shield, between any such controller and its environment that certifies a bound on the probability of reaching an unsafe condition during a bounded task. Given a predicate abstraction and candidate successor sets, everything else comes from logs: the loop becomes a finite controlled Markov chain, the estimated kernel is surrounded by a distribution-free confidence region, and robust reach-avoid value iteration runs over it. The certificate is probably approximately correct and uniform over controllers respecting the filter, so one model may replace another without recomputation. In all tested datasets the true risk stayed within certificate and budget; in a file-system sandbox the filter stays sound against a hazard the logs barely covered, where a plug-in baseline certifies safety and fails; and it holds seven controllers, three of them open-weights models, to zero unsafe outcomes in 1050 episodes.

Systems and Control.title: Tutorial on Aided Inertial Navigation Systems: A Modern Treatment Using Lie-Group Theoretical Methods
Systems and Control.summary:
Robots and autonomous vehicles rely on accurate estimates of their position, velocity, and orientation. Inertial sensors measure motion at high rates, but errors accumulate as these measurements are integrated. Satellite navigation, cameras, and other sensors help limit this drift. Combining these sources effectively requires estimation methods that account for the geometry of the navigation state.
  This tutorial presents a unified introduction to aided inertial navigation from a Lie-group perspective. It connects motion prediction, uncertainty propagation, and measurement updates within a common geometric framework. Particular attention is given to invariant filtering, which uses system symmetries to simplify the description and evolution of estimation errors. The tutorial explains how choices of state and error representations shape the filter equations. It connects theoretical principles with formulas suitable for implementation and discusses recent extensions addressing convergence and sensor biases. By organizing established and emerging methods around their shared geometric foundations, the presentation provides students, researchers, and engineers with a basis for understanding, implementing, and extending navigation algorithms.
Systems and Control.comment: Accepted in IEEE Control Systems Magazine

Systems and Control.title: Venusian Radio Occultation Constellation Design and Reconfiguration Problems: A Benders Decomposition Approach
Systems and Control.summary: Driven by the scientific value of Venusian atmospheric studies, numerous missions, such as Magellan and Venus Express, have relied on single-spacecraft radio occultation (RO) experiments. Despite their proven success, data throughput is inherently limited by the use of a single transmitter and its relative geometry with respect to Earth-based receivers. Therefore, the literature proposes leveraging a constellation of spacecraft to increase RO measurement opportunities and improve spatial and temporal coverage; however, current efforts impose strict simplifying assumptions that limit their applicability and responsiveness to complex mission narratives. Beyond initial constellation design, evolving mission objectives may require event-based constellation reconfiguration during operations. To address both design and operational needs, we propose two problems formulated as integer linear programs: the RO Constellation Configuration Design Problem and the RO Constellation Reconfiguration Problem. Further, we address the programs' solution-space explosion with a Benders decomposition approach. Numerical experiments show the applicability of our problems for constellation configuration design, tackle the full mission pipeline, transitioning from global atmospheric profiling to on-demand regional profiling above areas of volcanic interest, and show that the Benders decomposition approach efficiently obtains high-quality solutions to large-scale instances.
Systems and Control.comment: 36 pages

Systems and Control.title: DCCB-Capability-Aware Optimal Info-Power Flow for Transmission Switching in AC/MTDC Grids
Systems and Control.summary: Transmission switching is an effective approach for restoring operational flexibility and improving the economic performance of AC/multi-terminal DC (MTDC) grids following DC-side faults. Its practical implementation requires that the faulted branch be safely isolated and that the associated switching commands be successfully delivered through the communication network. However, conventional transmission switching models generally represent switching actions using binary variables, without considering the availability of communication resources or whether the corresponding DC circuit breakers (DCCBs) can interrupt the fault current affected by time delay. To address these issues, this paper develops an explicit optimal info--power flow (OIPF) formulation that incorporates information transmission into the post-fault transmission-switching optimization for AC/MTDC grids. The switching status of each DC branch is determined by the availability of its communication path and associated communication resources. In addition, binary switching decisions are supplemented by a DCCB feasibility constraint that limits the estimated delayed-interruption current to the DCCB breaking capability. The resulting problem is formulated as a mixed-integer second-order cone programming (MISOCP) model that can be efficiently solved using off-the-shelf optimization solvers. Numerical results reveal that limited communication capacity and additional routing costs may render electrically beneficial switching actions infeasible or uneconomical, while delay-aware DCCB interruption constraints may favor lower-delay communication routes despite their higher costs.

Systems and Control.title: Safeguarding Intelligent Power Dispatch:A Performance-Equivalent-Model-Based Safety-Critical Control Method for DC Microgrids
Systems and Control.summary: Intelligent power dispatch is enabling fast and self-adaptive decision-making in microgrids, yet its deployment in real-world industry remains limited due to unresolved safety concerns. Existing safety-preserving approaches typically rely on an accurate characterization of the feasible operating region, which is impossible to obtain under uncertain and heterogeneous system dynamics. Moreover, even a dispatch command verified as feasible at a discrete setpoint may become unsafe during its continuous physical execution. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a safety-aware dispatch adjustment framework that uses performance-equivalent modeling of closed-loop systems (PEM-CLS) and embeds high-order control barrier functions and control Lyapunov functions within a quadratic programming formulation (HOCBF-CLF-QP). PEM-CLS captures EMS-required power-regulation dynamics solely from port-level responses, without requiring internal subsystem models, parameters, or controller information. Its modeling error is analytically characterized and explicitly bounded, enabling requirement-oriented dynamic abstraction for safety-critical control. Based on these PEMs, the HOCBF-CLF-QP safety controller coordinates heterogeneous transient power responses and corrects unsafe EMS commands to maintain dynamic safety during command execution. Four deliberately constructed extreme stress-test scenarios are used to expose conflicts between nominal EMS commands and physical safety. Without intervention, the DC-bus voltage violates its safety limit in all four cases, whereas the proposed framework maintains QP feasibility and limits the voltage deviation. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides an algorithm-agnostic safety execution layer for intelligent power dispatch without requiring an exact feasible-region model or detailed internal information of lower-level devices.

Systems and Control.title: Distributed Stochastic Proximal Algorithm on Riemannian Submanifolds for Weakly-convex Functions
Systems and Control.summary: This paper aims to investigate the distributed stochastic optimization problems on compact embedded submanifolds (in the Euclidean space) where the local cost functions are weakly-convex. To address the manifold structure, we propose a distributed Riemannian stochastic proximal algorithm framework by utilizing the retraction and Riemannian consensus protocol, and analyze three specific algorithms: the distributed Riemannian stochastic subgradient, proximal point, and prox-linear algorithms. When the initial points satisfy certain conditions, we show that the iterates generated by this framework converge to a nearly stationary point in expectation while achieving consensus. We further establish the convergence rate of the algorithm framework as $\mathcal{O}(\frac{1+κ_g}{\sqrt{k}})$ where $k$ denotes the number of iterations and $κ_g$ shows the impact of manifold geometry on the algorithm performance. Finally, numerical experiments are implemented to demonstrate the theoretical results and show the empirical performance.

Systems and Control.title: NANO: A Unified Optimization Framework for Nonlinear Gaussian Filtering
Systems and Control.summary: Conventional Gaussian filtering typically approximates nonlinear models or their statistical moments and retains the Kalman update structure. The resulting approximation errors can affect both state estimates and their uncertainty. This paper presents the Natural Gradient Gaussian Approximation (NANO) framework for nonlinear filtering. Both prediction and measurement update are formulated as optimization problems over Gaussian distributions, with the entire Gaussian distribution serving as the optimization variable. The framework integrates observation losses, distributional discrepancies, natural-gradient optimization, and finite-step update rules, providing a unified formulation for constructing different filters. Natural-gradient iterations account for the geometry of the Gaussian family and jointly update the distribution parameters. The framework incorporates the existing NANO-P method using the Kullback-Leibler divergence and introduces NANO-W using the Wasserstein distance. NANO-P maintains covariance positive definiteness through a positive-semidefinite curvature approximation, while NANO-W uses a covariance transport update that accommodates indefinite curvature. Their update rules and sufficient conditions for covariance positive definiteness are established within the common framework. Through these two realizations, the proposed framework achieves the best estimation accuracy among the evaluated methods on each of six benchmarks. Runtime evaluations further assess its computational feasibility for practical applications.

Systems and Control.title: Scalable Identification of Physics-Based and Neural Dynamics from Partial Measurements
Systems and Control.summary: We present a scalable method for identifying nonlinear dynamics from partial measurements, supporting physics-based, neural-network, and gray-box models. We use the Prediction Error Method (PEM) coupled with state estimation performed by a Moving Horizon Estimation (MHE) scheme, which can account directly for general nonlinear dynamics. This results in a bi-level optimization problem that scales poorly with increasing model parameters. To improve computational efficiency, we derive a reformulation that avoids explicit parameter-wide sensitivity matrices and exploits the temporal structure of the underlying optimization problem. Numerical comparisons show up to a $215\times$ speedup in hypergradient evaluation. Racing-vehicle simulations demonstrate accurate prediction and physical-parameter recovery in tire-force identification. Real-world data show that the gray-box model improves prediction accuracy with a neural residual while retaining physical interpretability.
Systems and Control.comment: The code is available at https://github.com/YiboFrankZhou/Scalable-PEM-MHE

Systems and Control.title: Design of Privacy-Preserving Estimators Under Prior Information Exposure
Systems and Control.summary: State estimation is widely used in networked dynamical systems, but released estimates may inadvertently reveal sensitive information about private state variables. Existing privacy-preserving estimation frameworks often do not explicitly account for adversarial prior knowledge. Motivated by this gap, we study privacy-preserving state estimation for discrete-time linear stochastic systems under prior information exposure using pointwise maximal leakage (PML). We first reveal a privacy anti-optimality property of the Kalman filter: in the absence of additive release noise, the steady-state Kalman filter maximizes PML privacy leakage among the considered class of stable linear estimators. We further establish a nontrivial lower bound on the steady-state estimation error enforced by $(\varepsilon,δ)$-PML privacy. We then derive sufficient release-noise conditions that guarantee $(\varepsilon,δ)$-PML privacy, first for the Kalman filter and then for stable linear estimators. Finally, a convex semidefinite program is formulated for a joint design of the estimator gain and release noise covariance, providing a tractable privacy-preserving estimator with an explicit upper bound on the steady-state estimation error. Simulations on a source--load power system demonstrate the proposed privacy--utility tradeoff.

Systems and Control.title: Aerodynamic Promptness of Tilting-Propeller Multirotors
Systems and Control.summary: This work develops a geometric theory of aerodynamic promptness for multirotor platforms whose propeller directions depend on a smooth orientation-mechanism configuration. The actuator state consists of the actual signed propeller speeds and the mechanism configuration, and the nonlinear actuator map retains both the signed-quadratic propeller law and the configuration-dependent thrust directions. Constant direction maps represent fixed propellers, while shared dependence on mechanism coordinates represents mechanically coupled tilts. A Riemannian metric on the product actuator manifold compares propeller accelerations and orientation-mechanism rates through physically interpretable scales. Composing the actuator-map differential, the musical isomorphism induced by this metric, and the dual differential defines a task-rate authority map from wrench covectors to wrench-rate vectors. In fixed task coordinates, the square root of the determinant of its matrix defines aerodynamic promptness. Positive promptness is equivalent to local wrench-rate surjectivity, while the associated spectrum resolves directional authority and conditioning. The same construction yields the metric horizontal inverse, the orthogonal projector onto wrench-fiber directions, and task-preserving internal motions that regulate promptness without changing the instantaneous wrench. The construction is related intrinsically to dynamic feedback linearization and specialized to the independently tilting, radially arranged Holocopter and Voliro architectures, clarifying how their established allocation and rank constructions fit within the same actuator-manifold geometry.

Systems and Control.title: Learning Reachability-Based Safety Representations for Real-Time Robot Navigation in Unknown and Dynamic Environments
Systems and Control.summary: Safe robot navigation in unknown, dynamic environments requires more than geometric collision checking: a robot still far from an obstacle may be unable to avoid it because of its speed, orientation, or the obstacle's motion. Hamilton--Jacobi (HJ) reachability analysis captures this in a value function whose sign separates states that admit a safe continuation from those where collision is unavoidable, but computing it online for every newly observed environment is too expensive. This dissertation trains neural implicit representations offline on reachability solutions to give optimization-based controllers this information in real time. Since the value function never exceeds the constraint, it equals a directly computed constraint, such as a signed distance, minus a nonnegative dynamics correction. Learning only this correction keeps represented obstacles outside the predicted safe set despite approximation errors. The first two of five methods use the learned function as a terminal constraint in model predictive control, for static local environments and predicted obstacle motion. The next two use it as a barrier candidate in control barrier function safety filters, for static environments and, through pairwise barriers in relative coordinates, for a varying number of moving obstacles. Simulations and hardware experiments on ground and aerial robots show better collision avoidance than geometric and hand-designed baselines, especially for short horizons and moving obstacles. The fifth method replaces the grid-based offline solver, which limits the first four to low-dimensional models. For control-affine dynamics with polytopic inputs, the HJ Hamiltonian is maximized at a vertex, so a parallelizable tree search over vertex inputs can generate training labels. With a loss from the HJ variational inequality, these labels yield barrier candidates for systems with up to 13 states.

Systems and Control.title: Towards learning-enhanced solvers for multi-parametric optimization
Systems and Control.summary:
Neural networks (NNs) have been employed in various ways to accelerate the solution of multi-parametric optimization problems (OPs), which prominently arise in model predictive control (MPC). Early approaches focused on approximating the parametric solution (e.g., the optimal control law) directly by NNs. More recently, learning-based techniques have been used to emulate or enhance solver iterations. For the direct approximation of the parametric solution, it has been demonstrated that exploiting structural properties of the underlying OP facilitates the design of suitable NN architectures. In this paper, we show that structural analysis can also be leveraged to systematically integrate learning into classical optimization algorithms, thereby enhancing their performance.
  We formalize our concept for the case of multi-parametric quadratic programs (mpQPs), which frequently arise in linear-quadratic MPC, as a representative application. More precisely, we demonstrate that tailored NNs enable a parameter-dependent fine-tuning of the step sizes in a standard dual projected gradient scheme. The design of the NNs is guided by the observation that optimal step sizes, which permit obtaining the exact optimal solution in finitely many iterations, are piecewise constant functions over the parameter space (e.g., the state space in MPC). We establish key theoretical properties of the proposed approach and illustrate its effectiveness in a numerical case study.
Systems and Control.comment: 8 pages, 3 figures, to be published in the proceedings of the 65th IEEE Conference on Decision and Control (2026)

Systems and Control.title: Convex Chance-Constrained Stochastic Control under Uncertain Specifications with Application to Learning-Based Hybrid Powertrain Control
Systems and Control.summary: This paper proposes a strictly convex chance-constrained stochastic control framework that accounts for uncertainty in control specifications such as reference trajectories and operational constraints. Control inputs and risk allocation are jointly optimized under general, possibly non-Gaussian, uncertainties through sufficient deterministic conditions for probabilistic constraint satisfaction. A decreasing risk regularizer ensures existence and full use of the allowable risk. Under the stated regularity assumptions, the joint solution is unique and locally Lipschitz-continuous, supporting stable numerical optimization. The formulation is extended to learning-based exactly linearizable (EL) models through monotone state and input transformations. A hybrid powertrain example compares deterministic control, equal risk allocation, and optimized risk allocation with and without regularization in terms of charge sustaining, constraint violations, closed-loop cost, and solver time.
Systems and Control.comment: Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Control Systems Technology (TCST)

Systems and Control.title: Offline-Tuned Service-Aware TN-NTN Feeder Allocation for 6G Post-Disaster Service Resilience
Systems and Control.summary: Terrestrial network (TN) failures during disasters can overload surviving base stations (BSs) and disrupt emergency services. A non-terrestrial network (NTN) provides fallback, but its feeder link can become a bottleneck as users migrate. This paper studies post-disaster network resilience through service-priority-aware orchestration of constrained NTN feeder capacity in a post-failure snapshot. A lightweight Cross-Entropy Method (CEM) tunes feeder, offload, and user-ranking parameters offline, not as an online artificial intelligence (AI) controller. A Python system-level simulator sweeps operating regions under abstract TN-NTN link and queueing models. Gains depend on failure severity. At a 180-Mbps feeder under total TN outage, the proposed policy increases the absolute emergency-weighted continuity metric Cemg from 0.399 to 0.666 relative to the matched rule baseline with uniform feeder scaling (paired gain: 0.267; 95% bootstrap CI: [0.264, 0.271]); mild damage can reduce aggregate continuity. Offline CEM feeder-weight tuning further improves severe-failure continuity over fixed service priorities, whereas tuned offload and user ranking provide no detectable incremental gain.
Systems and Control.comment: 6 pages, 5 figures, 2026 Globecom

Systems and Control.title: Geometric Transition of Latent Dynamics in Intermittent Chaos: SVD-based Effective Dimension for Detection and Proactive Control
Systems and Control.summary: This paper investigates the geometric detection of latent dynamic transitions (where the latent space is defined as a finite-dimensional state space reconstructed via a delay-embedding Hankel matrix) in mutually coupled phase-locked loops (PLLs) exhibiting on-off intermittent chaos. We propose a data-driven approach to identify the transition of the effective dimension in latent dynamics as a precursor to physical bursting events. By applying Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) to a Hankel matrix constructed from high-resolution oversampled data, we extract the effective dimension that reflects the dynamical shift of intrinsic variables - from a synchronized two-dimensional manifold to a higher-dimensional chaotic state - prior to the actual burst. This geometric indicator enables a proactive, event-driven intervention using Pyragas-type delayed feedback control, which is activated only when the detected dimension exceeds a critical threshold. Simulation results demonstrate that this geometric precursor effectively compensates for control latencies and substantially reduces accumulated control energy compared to conventional continuous feedback. The findings establish a methodological strategy for stabilizing infinite-dimensional delayed systems by exploiting early warning signals embedded in dimensional transitions of latent dynamics.
Systems and Control.comment: 13 pages, 7 figures. Accepted for publication in Chaos: An Interdisciplinary Journal of Nonlinear Science

Systems and Control.title: Equilibria and consensus in discrete-time opinion dynamics with mixed weighted-averaging and weighted-median mechanisms
Systems and Control.summary: Opinion dynamics models relate interpersonal influence to consensus or persistent disagreement. We study a discrete-time model combining weighted-average and weighted-median updates on a fixed directed network. Individuals update synchronously with possibly different adjustment coefficients. We characterize equilibria through local balance conditions and opinion level sets, and establish convergence to a Lyapunov-stable equilibrium using nonexpansiveness and Krasnosel'skii--Mann theory. We define type-dependent cohesive sets: each weighted-average member assigns all its weight to the set, whereas each weighted-median member assigns at least one half. Consensus is reached from every initial condition if and only if no two such sets are disjoint. Otherwise, an open set of initial conditions leads to persistent disagreement. Replacing weighted-median individuals by weighted-average individuals preserves consensus whenever it is already guaranteed for all initial conditions. Four numerical studies examine the number and locations of weighted-average individuals. The frequency of reaching a prescribed consensus tolerance is nondecreasing with their fraction in the sampled ensembles, but individual realizations need not follow this trend.
Systems and Control.comment: 23 pages, 10 figures, including supplementary material

Systems and Control.title: Repeated Binary Direct Collinear Impacts Under Incremental Contact Laws With Permanent Indentation: A Hybrid Systems Formulation
Systems and Control.summary: Incremental contact laws specify the normal contact force through a differential equation carrying an internal state, driven by the indentation and its rate. In some, the force is extinguished at a nonzero indentation, whether by plastic deformation or by an elastic aftereffect, so that a residual deformation remains at the separation. Such laws sit uneasily within rigid body dynamics, which admits no deformation. The tension is tolerable when the indentation is small relative to the bodies, so that it may be carried constitutively rather than geometrically. Even then, the contact law alone does not determine the interaction of the bodies. Because force and indentation no longer vanish together, conditions for the commencement and termination of contact must be supplied separately. So must the fate of the deformation and internal state at separation, neither of which the equations of motion contain. This article formulates the repeated direct collinear impact of two convex bodies under external forces as a hybrid dynamical system. The contact interface is modeled as a massless element carrying the contact law and its state, coupled to the bodies through relative velocity and an interaction force dictated by the contact state. Consequently, all switching and resets are confined to the interface, leaving the geometry and the equations of motion of the bodies unaltered. The principal analytical properties of the resulting formulations are established, among them passivity and completeness; the branching of solutions at the onset and termination of contact is also examined. The framework is demonstrated through numerical simulations.
Systems and Control.comment: 28 pages, 6 figures

Systems and Control.title: Vector-field guided constraint-following control for path following of uncertain mechanical systems
Systems and Control.summary: Achieving dynamics-level control is a critical yet challenging problem for accurate, high-speed geometric path-following of uncertain robotic systems. This paper proposes a vector-field-guided constraint-following control framework for geometric path following of uncertain mechanical systems. The key idea is to encode vector-field guidance as a velocity constraint, enabling a unified force/torque control design for a class of fully actuated and underactuated systems with desired paths that may be self-intersecting. A global, explicit error estimate connects constraint-following accuracy to path-following performance, transferring convergence guarantees. An adaptive robust extension further addresses heterogeneous time-varying uncertainties with unknown bounds and ensures ultimately bounded path-following error. Applications to an underactuated aircraft system and a fully actuated manipulator system demonstrate the effectiveness and advantages of the framework.

Systems and Control.title: Stabilization of Nonlinear Systems with State-Dependent Representation: From Model-Based to Direct Data-Driven Control
Systems and Control.summary: This paper presents a framework for stabilizing nonlinear systems in state-dependent form. We first develop a model-based formulation that constructs a polytope enclosing the state-dependent system matrices over a prescribed state region and then synthesizes the controller by solving linear matrix inequalities (LMIs) at the polytope vertices. To establish stability and region of attraction (ROA) guarantees from the vertex LMIs, we develop a model-based mechanism and then apply it to direct data-driven control. In the data-driven setting, we use a known library of basis functions to represent the dynamics with unknown coefficients. A polytope captures the basis-function variation over a state region, and a data-consistent set characterizes the noise-induced coefficient uncertainty. This data-consistent set is incorporated directly into the vertex LMIs via Petersen's lemma. Building on our model-based mechanism, the resulting vertex LMIs yield a controller that guarantees stability and provides a certified ROA. The data-driven formulation further establishes disturbance-robustness guarantees and ROA estimates under input saturation. Numerical simulations and physical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed controller.

Systems and Control.title: $H_2$-optimal model order reduction using hyperbolic geometry
Systems and Control.summary: We revisit the problem of approximating a linear time-invariant LTI model by a reduced-order model (ROM) in an $H_2$-optimal sense. A widely used method for computing such ROMs is the iterative rational Krylov algorithm (IRKA). However, in practice, the stability of the resulting ROM is not generally guaranteed. In this work, we develop a novel framework that can be used to obtain $H_2$-optimal models of single-input single-output LTI systems while enforcing stability of the ROM. We use Malmquist-Takenaka orthogonal expansions in the corresponding $H_2$-spaces and their connection to hyperbolic geometry to develop an equilibrium function. We show that the poles of an $H_2$-optimal ROM transfer function are defined by the zeros of this equilibrium function. The resulting nonlinear root-finding problem is solved using a Newton-type method formulated on the products of Poincaré disk manifolds, where updates are performed along hyperbolic geodesics ensuring that the stability constraint is satisfied at every iteration. We present numerical experiments on benchmark systems for both discrete- and continuous-time LTI MOR problems, including examples where IRKA produces unstable reduced models while the proposed method preserves stability throughout the iteration.

Systems and Control.title: Event-Driven Safe Control of a Black-Box Balancing Wheel with Friction-Gated Actuation
Systems and Control.summary: Commercial balancing wheels are closed systems: an internal controller keeps the board upright, and a rider steers by shifting weight and twisting the hips. We augment a one-wheel with a lead-screw weight shift for longitudinal motion and a reaction wheel for yaw. The reaction wheel stores limited momentum, so a turn is a sequence of torque pulses, and whether a pulse rotates the body depends on static friction at the tire contact. From a 24-pulse torque sweep on one surface we fit a two-part model that gives the probability that a pulse rotates the body, treating the breakaway torque as random, and the rotation angle when it does; at maximum torque the posterior engagement probability is 0.54 (90% credible interval 0.24-0.84). The weight shift is modeled as a rate- limited input with a measured speed gain and an assumed first-order response, which predicts stopping distances four times those of a direct-force model. These models drive an event-triggered supervisor that schedules pulses by expected heading improvement, brakes when the predicted braking path would leave the safe set, tightens margins for model uncertainty, and updates the friction estimate online. In simulation on 500 plants drawn from the fitted models, the robust supervisor completed 92.6% of missions with 1.8% safety violations and 1.6% safe aborts, versus 84.0% and 7.2% for a supervisor using mean models and 1.8% and 20.4% for a baseline that ignores friction. A video of the hardware experiments is available online (https://github.com/ASAS-Labs/x-wheel).

Systems and Control.title: Adaptive Calibration of Day-Ahead Flexibility Reserve Requirements Under Distribution Shift
Systems and Control.summary: The increasing integration of variable renewable generation introduces weather-driven variability and uncertainty into power-system operations. System operators manage the resulting deviations between day-ahead forecasts and real-time net load by scheduling upward and downward flexibility reserves. These requirements have traditionally been set using simple deterministic rules. Newer data-driven methods tailor reserves to forecasts and operating conditions. However, their reliability may deteriorate when conditions depart from the historical data. We address this limitation with a sequential framework that updates day-ahead reserve requirements as operating outcomes become available. Within this framework, Adaptive Conformal Inference targets the frequency of insufficient reserve, whereas Rolling Risk Control targets expected uncovered deviation, the mean residual beyond the scheduled reserve. We prove finite-horizon bounds on realized miscoverage and capped uncovered-deviation loss. We test the framework on real ERCOT data in a chronological deployment simulation that respects operational timing: outcomes from one day first affect the reserve schedule two days later. Training and validation use 2022--2023 data; the uninterrupted test covers 2024--2025. Coverage calibration achieves approximately 90% coverage, with upward and downward miscoverage near 5%. Risk calibration brings expected uncovered deviations close to their budgets while using 5.3% less reserve than the uncalibrated requirements. The framework thus produces adaptive reserve requirements that provably control the selected reliability metrics over finite horizons without assuming stationarity or exchangeability.

Systems and Control.title: AC-Aware Steady-State Security Region Characterization via Exclusion Refinement
Systems and Control.summary: As active power dispatch becomes increasingly coupled with reactive power support and voltage security in modern power systems, AC security regions (AC-SRs) under exact steady-state AC power flow (AC-PF) constraints provide valuable insights into admissible operating boundaries and security margins for security assessment. However, the nonconvexity of exact AC-PF constraints makes it difficult to achieve both accuracy and computational efficiency in AC-SR characterization. To this end, this paper proposes an AC-aware iterative exclusion refinement (AC-ITER) approach that refines a given convex-relaxed AC-SR toward the exact AC-SR by progressively constructing and removing convexlocal exclusion subregions around numerically identified insecure points. Boundary-point searches and dual-based local exclusion cuts provide a tractable approximation of relaxation-induced insecure portions. A statistical certification method based on uniform sampling is developed to support high-confidence assessment of residual-region security and guide termination, while an AC-PF security similarity-based acceleration (AC-SSA) approach is introduced to further accelerate the sampling-based search for insecure operating points. Numerical studies on academic test systems and real-world systems demonstrate the characterization accuracy of AC-ITER and the computational efficiency gained through AC-SSA.

Systems and Control.title: GPU-Accelerated Quantum Annealing-Inspired UAV Path Planning for Smart Agriculture
Systems and Control.summary: With the rapid advancement of smart agriculture, Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) have become indispensable for efficient coverage and path planning in grid-mapped agricultural fields. However, optimizing UAV flight paths in large-scale environments remains a complex Nondeterministic Polynomial-time (NP)-hard problem. Traditional path planning methods are often constrained by local optima, limited scalability, and slow convergence, which significantly restrict their effectiveness in solving large-scale problems. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a novel optimization framework utilizing a Graphics Processing Unit (GPU)-parallelized Ising solver. Our method mimics the operational principles of quantum annealing on GPU hardware, enabling rapid search for the minimum-energy state of Ising models. Unlike physical quantum devices, which are often constrained by the number of qubits, our approach leverages the Fixstars Amplify (FA) platform to perform parallel annealing on highly parallelized GPUs. This enables the simultaneous evaluation of thousands of potential path candidates and vast state transitions. By leveraging large-scale parallel processing, this framework's core strength lies in minimizing computation time even as the problem scale increases. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposed method consistently identifies superior flight paths while maintaining stable computational performance compared with the genetic algorithm and simulated annealing method.
Systems and Control.comment: 6 pages, 3 figures, conference

Systems and Control.title: CIPHEUR: LLM-Guided Structural Search Control for Conflict-Graph Optimization
Systems and Control.summary: Conflict-graph search can stagnate despite effective operators when interventions fail to address the conflicts blocking progress. A disruptive intervention may also require further search before its value emerges. We propose CIPHEUR, a large language model (LLM)-guided framework that connects conflict evidence to coordinated intervention and recovery through Structured Intervention Units (SIUs). The shared control interface supports offline synthesis of executable policies and online contextual decisions. Asynchronous online control sustains native search during inference, while all policies preserve the original objective and feasibility constraints. Across eight satellite-ground scheduling conflict views with five runs per view and a 900-second evaluation cap, CIPHEUR-online achieves the highest mean objective among 11 configurations and increases mean scheduled contact duration by 14.84% over the greedy baseline GWMIN. It exceeds the strongest external per-view mean in seven of eight views and outperforms CHILS in all 40 paired runs. Within the same runs, its normalized objective improvement from 360 to 900 seconds is 1.50 to 1.86 times that of the two programmatic controllers. A separately frozen, one-shot LLM-generated controller also improves the mean objective over CHILS without runtime model calls. Together, these results demonstrate how structural search control translates LLM design knowledge and contextual reasoning into improved solution quality and sustained search progress.

Human-Computer Interaction.title: A Mechanomyography-Based Integrated Sensing-Stimulation System for Fatigue-Aware Neuromuscular Therapy
Human-Computer Interaction.summary: Muscle fatigue limits the effectiveness of functional electrical stimulation (FES), yet fatigue monitoring during active stimulation remains challenging because electromyography (EMG) is severely contaminated by stimulation artifacts. To address this issue, this study proposes an integrated mechanomyography-based sensing framework (MMG-FES) for artifact-resistant fatigue monitoring during stimulation. Fatigue states were first characterized during voluntary movement using established EMG spectral indicators, including median frequency (MF) and mean power frequency (MPF), and then linked to MMG-derived features, including high-frequency energy ratio (HFER) and spectral bandwidth (BW), for fatigue recognition under stimulation conditions. Experimental results showed consistent fatigue-related trends, with EMG spectral features decreasing and MMG features exhibiting coordinated spectral redistribution across repeated contractions. Using these features, the proposed framework achieved fatigue-state recognition accuracies of 0.93 and 0.96 with logistic regression and random forest, respectively. These findings support MMG as a physiologically meaningful and stimulation-compatible modality for fatigue-aware closed-loop neuromuscular stimulation.
Human-Computer Interaction.comment: 12 pages, 14 figures

Human-Computer Interaction.title: Vision: "What Don't I Know About User's Preferences?" How Uncertainty Estimation Improves Proactive Assistant Alignment
Human-Computer Interaction.summary: Proactive Smart Assistants (PSAs) increasingly use general knowledge, learned patterns from group-level data, patterns from individual user's data, and recent sensor observations to anticipate which action a user may prefer. Existing systems typically select actions from predicted user preference likelihoods, but these likelihoods alone do not reveal how reliable the prediction is, which evidence supports it, or why ambiguity remains. In this vision paper, we argue that uncertainty estimation can provide this missing information and substantially change appropriate downstream behavior. Using the example of a home assistant, we introduce the questions that uncertainty estimation aims to answer, i.e. how sure is the assistant about the predicted preference likelihood, whether the confidence come from group-level assumptions or individual's data, and whether likelihood ambiguity reflect the user's intrinsic preference variability or insufficient data for the particular situation. We further introduce uncertainty estimation applications in neighboring domains, such as human trajectory prediction, personalized activity recognition, information-collection, and model-based control. Finally, we draw on insights from neighboring domains to envision how future uncertainty-aware proactive assistants may address key challenges in proactive interaction.
Human-Computer Interaction.comment: Published in Companion of the 2026 ACM International Joint Conference on Pervasive and Ubiquitous Computing (UbiComp Companion '26) PEACE Workshop

Human-Computer Interaction.title: Navigating the Conceptual Multiverse
Human-Computer Interaction.summary: When language models answer open-ended questions, they implicitly make decisions that shape their answers. However, the models do not show these decisions to the user, so users cannot contextualize answers: they cannot see the assumptions an answer rests on or the alternatives to it. Drawing on multiverse analysis from statistics, we introduce the conceptual multiverse, a representation in which language models express answers as the result of intermediate conceptual decisions. We build a system that generates such decisions explicitly, organizes them into a space of answers that users can see and change, and checks them against the norms of a specific domain. In a user study across three domains - philosophy, AI alignment annotation, and poetry - participants say that our system helps them see the decisions leading to an answer, explore the space of answers, and understand the decisions structuring this space.

Human-Computer Interaction.title: FreeBrush: Motor Signals-Based Toothbrushing Monitoring System for Electric Toothbrushes
Human-Computer Interaction.summary: Oral health is vital for overall well-being, yet many users brush different tooth surfaces for insufficient or excessive durations. Toothbrushing monitoring systems can help improve brushing habits by reminding users of under-brushed and over-brushed surfaces, but existing approaches often rely on external sensors, increasing cost and reducing practicality. We observe that the intrinsic motor signals of electric toothbrushes can reflect the brushing surfaces and durations. When brushing different tooth surfaces, the brush head experiences different constraints from the surrounding oral cavity, changing the motor's driving currents and position feedback. Based on this observation, we propose FreeBrush, a toothbrushing monitoring system that uses the intrinsic motor signals of electric toothbrushes to recognize brushed tooth surfaces and estimate brushing durations without any external sensors. We prototype the system on a commercial off-the-shelf electric toothbrush and conduct a comprehensive evaluation with 18 participants. FreeBrush achieves 92.8% accuracy for 16-surface recognition and 92.0% accuracy for brushing duration estimation. The system further shows robustness across different toothpastes, brush heads, vibration modes, usage scenarios, and long-term use, and is capable of running on edge devices. By recognizing brushed tooth surfaces and estimating the brushing duration, FreeBrush can help users identify under-brushed and over-brushed surfaces and build balanced brushing habits.
Human-Computer Interaction.comment: 15 pages. Includes a 2-page supplementary document as an ancillary file. Extended version of our workshop paper "BrushSense: Toothbrushing Region Recognition Using Motor Signals" (UbiSense 2026)

Human-Computer Interaction.title: Configuring AI for Exploratory Learning: Educator Perspectives on Inference, Persistence, and Disclosure
Human-Computer Interaction.summary: Generative AI (GenAI) can support open-ended learning through generation, personalization, and learner modeling, yet educators need ways to shape these capabilities around educational goals. Through interviews and design activities with 15 U.S. educators, we examined educator configuration of GenAI using K-12 career exploration as an exploratory context. Educators configured not only AI-generated experiences, but also when student activity became an inference, whether learner information persisted, who could access it, and how it informed subsequent human action. They also faced challenges translating teaching needs into configurations: recognizing possibilities for control beyond familiar uses of GenAI, decomposing general-purpose AI into understandable functions and responsibilities, and identifying useful information through intended teaching actions. We discuss how GenAI systems can support educators in expressing and testing configurations, while establishing boundaries around personalization, inference, persistence, disclosure, and action to keep AI-supported learning aligned with evolving learner needs.
Human-Computer Interaction.comment: 32 pages

Human-Computer Interaction.title: COSI-Lab: Conference Living Lab for Modeling Multi-Perspective Multimodal Social Intention
Human-Computer Interaction.summary: COSI-Lab presents a multimodal multi-sensor dataset of a real interdisciplinary scientific workshop with 32 academics at an international conference. It captures ecologically valid social interactions in a weakly scripted setting consisting of two 30-minute mingling sessions with real professional and social consequences. We argue that intelligent systems could better handle subjective perceptions by modeling their multiplicity not as label noise but as an explainable perspective-driven reasoning process. We focus on the Apparent Intent Inference (AII) problem as determined by ex-situ observers and conceptualize intentions to be independent of the future. We contribute a novel annotation process for AII that accounts for a perceiver's own interpretative tendencies, quantitative and qualitative analyses of intent narratives with respect to diversity, plausibility and grounding, benchmark tasks for AII and relevant contextual factors, speech quality audio for all participants as well as privacy-preserving multi-modal environmental and wearable sensor data, enabling lexical and nonverbal behavior analysis; and the coupling of self-reported participant goals (30 minute to 3 hour) with annotated AII (seconds).

Human-Computer Interaction.title: CoBG: Learning from Player Reviews to Design, Critique, and Revise Board Game Rulebooks
Human-Computer Interaction.summary: Board game design alternates between thinking as a designer and experiencing as a player, over repeated cycles of prototyping, critique, and revision. This loop is cognitively demanding: without knowing how players will receive a rule, a designer cannot tell what to revise. We present CoBG, a design assistant that supports this workflow end to end with four modules that learn from 2.2K structured rulebooks and 180K player reviews: BG-Ideator turns multi-turn dialogue into a structured design draft; BG-Realizer writes a rulebook and revises it with BG-Critic, a review-grounded critic that localizes flaws along the Mechanics-Dynamics-Aesthetics chain and accepts a revision only when it prefers it; and BG-Persona previews feedback from 150 profiled reviewers. On 207 held-out games, CoBG localizes flaws in rulebooks and revises them better than general-purpose LLMs, and iterative revision brings their rating close to that of published rulebooks. Blind readers prefer CoBG's rulebooks to GPT-5.4's in 38 of 50 new design intents under the same revision budget. In a 30-participant user study and paper-prototype playtests, designers using CoBG report less blank-page anxiety and catch flaws they would otherwise miss, and the resulting rulebooks hold up at the table with few rule breakdowns.

Human-Computer Interaction.title: A Co-Located MMG-FES Wearable Interface for Action-Updated State-Gated Stimulation
Human-Computer Interaction.summary: Functional electrical stimulation (FES) assists movement, but fixed schedules cannot track how a repeatedly activated muscle changes, and surface electromyography (EMG) near the stimulation electrodes is often obscured by artifacts. Prior work recorded mechanomyography (MMG) passively during closed-loop FES cycling and estimated FES-induced fatigue or predicted fatigue for FES control, without gating stimulation with stimulated-site MMG. In this study, we present VG-FES, a wearable module co-locating microphone-based MMG, programmable charge-balanced biphasic stimulation, and embedded state-gated control at one on-skin thigh site. After each action, we compare rectus femoris (RF) mean power frequency (MPF) with an early-session baseline of the same direction, giving a relative state. A threshold on its window means enables fixed-duration bursts separated by rest periods. During onboard stimulation, MMG remained recordable, whereas near-site EMG was artifact-dominated. Under prolonged external stimulation, cycle-wise MMG tracked an independent local-pressure reference (Spearman rho = 0.968). In leave-one-session-out evaluation on 2284 squat actions (11 sessions, eight participants), MMG-based action segmentation reached an event-detection F1 of 0.923 and direction classification a balanced accuracy of 0.925. Online, over 15.69 min of self-paced squats, one participant received four bursts while MMG acquisition and action monitoring continued. Mechanical feedback from the stimulated site offers wearable FES and assistive robotics a per-action basis for state-gated stimulation.
Human-Computer Interaction.comment: 9 pages, 8 figures. Submitted to IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters

Human-Computer Interaction.title: Side-Vent Design for Microphone-Based Mechanomyography Sensors: Modeling and Experimental Evaluation of Contact Dependence
Human-Computer Interaction.summary: Wearable muscle sensing for rehabilitation, assistive robotics, and electrical-stimulation feedback needs mechanomyography sensors less sensitive to fit changes during wear. In microphone-based mechanomyography, cavity pressure depends on rim contact, a dependence housing design has rarely targeted. This study evaluates a side-vented housing, whose vent opens a pressure-relief path in parallel with the rim to lower contact dependence, and quantifies the acoustic-gain cost. Thermoviscous finite-element simulations compared twenty cavity configurations under prescribed source motion. Paired bench sweeps over 10-200 Hz on both housings compared direct contact with a Gap-ring spacer, a radially grooved spacer ring. At 100 Hz, side venting reduced the simulated acoustic-gain variation across 0.10-0.50 mm rim clearances from 25.8 to 10.0 dB and cost 5.5 dB of gain at 0.20 mm clearance. Velocity fields and branch-flow calculations identified this path. At the higher speaker drive level, the Gap-ring spacer caused median attenuations of 13.6 dB (vented) and 30.1 dB (unvented) relative to direct contact. In this front end, a 35.9-dB signal-gain increase at 100 Hz raised the calculated operational-amplifier voltage-noise gain by 1.6 dB. A single-participant demonstration of paced elbow flexion and extension compared envelope timing and spectra between housings, finding similar envelope timing (correlation 0.935) and broadly similar spectra (correlation 0.956). Vent area trades acoustic gain against contact dependence and can therefore serve as a housing design parameter.
Human-Computer Interaction.comment: 10 pages, 9 figures, 1 table. Submitted to IEEE Sensors Journal

Human-Computer Interaction.title: A Benchmark for Spatially Grounded Gesture Generation
Human-Computer Interaction.summary: Communication in shared space interweaves verbal and non-verbal signals, and pointing gestures anchor language to the environment: "put the cup on that one" is uninterpretable without the gesture that fixes the referent. Yet no common framework exists for evaluating whether generated gestures indicate their intended referent; distributional metrics reward a gesture aimed at the wrong object as long as it looks natural. We introduce a benchmark for spatially grounded gesture generation, comprising ~2K pointing-annotated clips from naturalistic VR dialogue with ground-truth 3D referents, a task in which systems must decide when, how and where to point within conversational speech, and a protocol that separates temporal alignment, spatial grounding and perceived naturalness. We also provide a flow-matching baseline, MM-Conv-Flow. Evaluating it alongside an independent retrieval-based system and captured human motion, we find that geometric grounding can exceed that of human pointing without any gain in perceived naturalness, showing that referential gesture quality must be measured along separate dimensions.
Human-Computer Interaction.comment: 13 pages, 9 figures. Benchmark of the Referential Gesture Challenge at the HSI Workshop, ECCV 2026. Data and video: https://huggingface.co/datasets/hsi-workshop/referential-gesture-challenge, v2: corrected references

Human-Computer Interaction.title: AuthScribe: Supporting Agency and Authorship in LLM-Assisted Reflective Journaling
Human-Computer Interaction.summary: Large language models are increasingly used in reflective journaling, where articulating an experience is part of interpreting it. This raises questions about how writers retain authorship, exercise agency, and assess personalized assistance. We present AuthScribe, an LLM-assisted reflective journaling system that combines contextual anchors, writer-steered AI support, Autobiographical Citations, and read-only Provisional Drafts that require re-expression before AI-generated suggestions enter the journal. Retrieval and LLM inference run on-device. In a 14-day field deployment with 14 participants, grounding shifted from situating current experiences to reconnecting them with prior self-authored interpretations. Perceived agency remained stable through Week 1 and shifted during Week 2. Participants described authorship through transforming AI-generated suggestions into personally meaningful expression, and trusted personalized prompts when they could trace them to prior writing. We discuss design implications for adoption friction, longitudinal agency, and traceable personalization in AI systems for personal reflection.

Human-Computer Interaction.title: "We Need a Standard": Toward an Expert-Informed Privacy Label for Differential Privacy
Human-Computer Interaction.summary: The increasing adoption of differential privacy (DP) leads to public-facing DP deployments by both government agencies and companies. However, real-world DP deployments often do not fully disclose their privacy guarantees, which vary greatly between deployments. Failure to disclose certain DP parameters can lead to misunderstandings about the strength of the privacy guarantee, undermining the trust in DP. In this work, we seek to inform future standards for communicating the privacy guarantees of DP deployments. Based on semi-structured interviews with 12 DP experts, we identify important DP parameters to communicate privacy guarantees for transparency and trust. We further elaborate why and how these parameters should be disclosed according to expert consensus.
Human-Computer Interaction.comment: 13 pages, 5 figures

Human-Computer Interaction.title: ArguScale: Evidence-Grounded Human-AI Sensemaking Across Concurrent Live Conversations
Human-Computer Interaction.summary: Monitoring concurrent classroom collaborative reasoning discussions is challenging because instructors have to track collaboration-relevant behaviors across multiple ongoing conversations at once. Existing Human-AI conversational sensemaking systems can scale monitoring upward through summaries and visual abstractions, but these representations may distance users from underlying conversational evidence, e.g., relevant audio and transcript segments, needed to forage downward. Through our formative study, we developed ArguScale, an evidence-grounded Human-AI sensemaking system that organizes interactional signals into temporally aligned representations linked to transcript and audio evidence. A temporal signal-density view provides temporal context and supports rapid cross-group comparison, while selective evidence access allows instructors to inspect audio and transcript. We evaluated ArguScale in a mixed-design study with 20 participants. Compared to other conditions, ArguScale improved participants' ability to efficiently and accurately identify collaboration-relevant cues. We further identify strategies participants used to forage for and make sense of conversational evidence under live time constraints.

Software Engineering.title: Small but Mighty: Test Suites as Improvement Signals for Self-Evolving Agents
Software Engineering.summary: A self-evolving agent rewrites its own harness and must decide which rewrites to keep, so its improvement signal is the check a rewrite has to pass. Verifying a rewrite by agent rollout is expensive and subjective, while executable checks such as the repository's own tests are too sparse to catch behavior-changing rewrites, rejecting only a quarter of them. We instead take test feedback as the executable signal, and search for test suites that are both small and strong with a quality-diversity evolutionary algorithm, so that the signal is dense and informative. TeSearch treats suite size as a behavior descriptor, so that quality is pursued at every size and a small, strong suite is reachable, and learns a transition kernel during the search that denoises the LLM as an actuator on that descriptor. Across 129 real-world modules and three backbones, TeSearch delivers the highest-quality suites of any method compared, LLM-driven evolutionary search included, and the smallest of any LLM-based one. Used as the improvement signal of a self-evolving agent, it rejects 59.9% of behavior-changing rewrites against 25.3% for the repository's tests, at a 4.0% false-alarm rate and 3.5 s per decision. The code and data are available at https://github.com/ccsnow127/TeSearch.
Software Engineering.comment: In NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Self-Evolving Diversity-Driven Search for Robust AI Systems (EvoRobust)

Software Engineering.title: BRQGen: Towards Adaptive Completeness Assessment and Follow-Up Question Generation for Bug Reports
Software Engineering.summary: Many bug reports lack the necessary information required to reproduce issues. In early studies, large language models have been employed to generate follow-up questions to enhance incomplete reports. However, they ask a fixed number of questions regardless of whether the report is incomplete. We propose BRQGen, an iterative framework that identifies missing or ambiguous information in bug reports and generates targeted follow-up questions, only if necessary. Reports with no identified gaps are classified as sufficient. When the author responds, BRQGen evaluates whether the answers provide the requested information and generates further questions for any exposed gaps. We curated a novel dataset of 429 incomplete bug reports from Home Assistant and Brave Browser, each containing at least one maintainer follow-up question. Each question is mapped to the author's answer and assigned a label indicating whether the requested information could have been provided directly through the issue template. Earlier maintainer requests were associated with author responses, whereas delayed requests were associated with no response. Among responding authors, requests within one hour received median replies after 0.52 hours in Home Assistant and 1.45 hours in Brave, versus 9.76 and 13.49 hours after four hours. BRQGen covered 35.4% (Qwen 3.8 Flash) to 51.8% (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash) of the 1,073 ground-truth follow-up questions. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash managed to ask 45.7% of all detailed questions and 63.9% of all generic questions. Gemini 3 Flash Preview reached the highest macro-F1 for completeness assessment of 49.3%, but with a post-hoc analysis by getting only the gaps with high severities, Qwen 3.8 Flash reaches 73.6% macro-F1 score. Completeness assessment improved when at least one identified gap had high severity, and nearly all ground-truth questions were captured within the first two iterations.

Software Engineering.title: Make Every Expansion Count: Learning to Search Efficiently in LLM Code Repair
Software Engineering.summary: Large language model (LLM) code-repair systems fix faulty programs by repeatedly generating and testing revisions. Each revision is costly, making the choice of which repair to pursue important for efficiency. Existing search policies rely on test pass rates and search statistics, ignoring the details of test failures and proposed edits. We introduce CodeTriage, a learned policy that prioritizes edits before their revised programs are generated and tested. Its 0.6B-parameter model reads the test output, failure diagnosis, and proposed edit, then predicts a distribution over the number of repair steps needed to reach a fix through that edit. These predictions prioritize all pending edits across programs before generating and testing the revised code. On held-out repair tasks, CodeTriage finds fixes with 21% fewer program revisions and 12% fewer output tokens than the strongest baseline on each metric. Without retraining, it achieves the highest average success across search budgets for each of 11 unseen repair LLMs. Ablations show that both the failure context and edit text, as well as comparisons across programs, improve search. We also release a corpus of 12.2 million program versions from four LLMs, organized into repair trees with proposed edits and test results.

Software Engineering.title: CUJBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Browser-to-Backend Failure Diagnosis
Software Engineering.summary: Automated failure diagnosis requires correlating browser-visible symptoms with backend observability signals, yet existing benchmarks do not evaluate this cross-modal reasoning task. Constructing one is non-trivial: multi-modal failure scenarios are costly to annotate, and live-environment capture introduces stochasticity that makes cross-run agent comparison unreliable. We present CUJBench, to our knowledge, the first benchmark to combine browser-visible failure evidence with backend observability in a diagnostic framing. CUJBench addresses annotation cost through an LLM-assisted generation pipeline with a multi-agent review loop and a three-layer annotation scheme, producing 87 labeled scenarios across five fault families, and ensures reproducibility by packaging each failure as a deterministic multi-modal snapshot with a fixed tool interface. Evaluating six LLMs under retrieval, browser-only, and full-toolset baselines, the benchmark yields an overall accuracy of 21.6% with a ceiling of 52.5%, well below saturation. Contrary to expectation, browser-only agents outperform full-toolset agents in aggregate, with expanded evidence access inducing unfocused exploration rather than improved synthesis. Trajectory analysis identifies cross-modal synthesis as the primary bottleneck: agents retrieve the decisive evidence but fail to attribute it correctly, a failure that persists across all six models and that model scale and richer tool access alone cannot resolve.

Software Engineering.title: Separating Statistical Inference from Experimental Runtime: An Architecture for Sequential Scientific Analysis
Software Engineering.summary: Sequential statistical procedures are increasingly embedded in scientific systems in which observations arrive incrementally from heterogeneous sources. In such systems the statistical update is only one part of the computation: observations must also be acquired, aligned across inputs, ordered, delivered, persisted, and replayed, and results must be passed to systems that display them or act on them. Sequential methods are nevertheless missing from the general software toolkit. They run inside proprietary experimentation platforms and commercial statistical packages, or exist as offline functions over complete data, and the batch fit interface that dominates machine-learning libraries has no place for a procedure that listens, keeps state, and decides when to stop. We propose an architecture that separates statistical inference from data topology, execution runtime, run lifecycle, persistence, and external action. Its central abstraction is the Sequential Procedure: a state-transition function that maps an inferential state, a valid statistical input, and a statistical random state to a new state and a scientific output. The procedure does not define how observations are acquired, paired, scheduled, stored, or acted upon. We specify the architecture semantically rather than through an object model, derive seven conformance invariants that any implementation can be tested against (among them synchronous/asynchronous, checkpoint, replay, and batch equivalence), and describe a dependency-free reference implementation in which all seven hold bitwise. Lorden's 2-SPRT for the Kiefer-Weiss problem serves as the reference procedure; the same contract accommodates sequential estimators, Bayesian filters, change-point detectors, and stateful predictive models.

Software Engineering.title: TENET: One Step Toward Test-Driven Development for Repository-Level Code Generation
Software Engineering.summary: Test-Driven Development (TDD) is a widely adopted practice that requires developers to create and execute tests alongside implementation. With recent advances in Large Language Models (LLMs), developers can shift from manually writing the code to defining tests as executable specifications and delegating code synthesis to AI agents. However, enabling repository-level TDD under developer-written tests is challenging, requiring: (1) specification enhancement: identifying a concise yet representative test subset from large suites with rich task semantics; (2) retrieval augmentation: using tests to guide reasoning and context retrieval; and (3) test-driven refinement: interpreting test feedback for iterative improvement. We propose TENET, an agentic framework for repository-level code generation under the TDD paradigm. TENET includes: (1) a test harness mechanism that selects a concise test suite to maximize diversity of the target usage scenarios; (2) a tailored agent toolset for efficient retrieval and debugging; and (3) a reflection-based refinement workflow that iteratively analyzes failures and updates implementations. TENET consistently outperforms the strongest baselines across backbones, achieving 69.08% and 81.77% Pass@1 on RepoCod and RepoEval with Claude Sonnet 4, improving by 9.49 and 2.17 percentage points, respectively. Additionally, we present the first systematic study of how test suite characteristics influence LLM agent performance in TDD settings.
Software Engineering.comment: Accepted at the 37th IEEE International Symposium on Software Reliability Engineering (ISSRE 2026)

Software Engineering.title: The Import Tax: A Longitudinal Measurement of Startup Cost in the Python Ecosystem
Software Engineering.summary: Python programs pay for their imports at every process start, a cost that is invisible in steady-state benchmarks but dominant for command-line tools, test workers, and serverless cold starts. Python 3.15 adds explicit lazy imports (PEP 810) on largely anecdotal evidence. We measure the import cost of the 500 most-downloaded PyPI packages, every quarterly release since mid-2021, under six CPython versions (3.9-3.14) on two platforms (Apple M5/macOS and Intel Xeon/Linux): all 66,816 package-version-interpreter cells, plus the release histories of 65 distributions beneath shared namespaces, and targeted experiments that isolate individual effects. Import cost is heavily skewed (median 12.3 ms, 99th percentile 400 ms on macOS). For the median package, 68-79% of import time is spent importing the standard library, while third-party dependencies are the largest component in the slowest decile. The cold first import is almost entirely bytecode compilation on Linux, but on macOS 67% of the cold penalty remains when bytecode is precompiled: we trace it to the operating system's security assessment of each new native library, which every fresh environment pays again. A package's own import code grows by a median 4.0-5.0% per year; resolving dependencies as of each release raises the median trend of the total from 1.8% to 3.0-3.4% per year. CPython 3.14 executes package code faster than 3.9 but imports more and slower standard-library modules, a net 1.16x slowdown on macOS and 1.07x on Linux. What dependents actually import from a package costs a median 1.0x its top-level import but 10.9-13.4x at the 90th percentile. Global lazy mode makes import statements essentially free and breaks 10 packages. Harness, analysis code, and dataset are public.
Software Engineering.comment: 20 pages, 6 figures, 2 tables. v2: revised and extended (complete coverage, namespace-package histories, dependency drift on both platforms, trace-based attribution, macOS cold-start mechanism, usage-weighted submodule cost, CPython 3.15rc3 lazy-import census). Dataset and code: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23300556

Software Engineering.title: Grounding Deep Learning Framework Testing in Data Flow
Software Engineering.summary: Data flow underlies deep learning (DL) framework execution, including automatic differentiation and operator-fusion optimization. Bugs involving data flow can cause incorrect results or unexpected behavior. Existing testing methods represent models primarily by operator topology, omitting runtime tensor values and properties and operator input requirements. They therefore cannot distinguish data flows in models with similar topologies, even when these differences affect framework behavior. We introduce the Tensor Flow Graph (TFG) to capture runtime tensor states and operator input requirements. Its nodes represent operators and their input requirements, while its edges record tensor values and properties. Building on the TFG, we propose FlowMuT, a mutation-based testing method grounded in data flow. Mutations are represented as constrained subgraph replacements, with mutation operators derived from prior work and an analysis of mutable data flow objects. In each round, FlowMuT builds a TFG for the seed model, pairs mutation operators with TFG sites, and filters illegal candidates using data flow constraints. It uses LinUCB to select a candidate based on coverage and impact, executes the mutant, updates selection feedback, and uses each accepted mutant as the next seed. We evaluate FlowMuT on PyTorch and MindSpore using representative models from diverse application scenarios. FlowMuT submitted 55 bug reports for cases missed by all baseline methods; developers confirmed 41 reports and fixed the bugs described in 7 reports. FlowMuT achieves 43.4% higher data flow diversity than the strongest baseline and a legal mutant rate of 96.7%, compared with 86.4% without constraints. These results show that testing from a data flow perspective is practical and effective.

Software Engineering.title: Passing Tests, Missing Semantics: Evidence of Interpretive Lock-In in Plan-Based DataFrame Code Generation
Software Engineering.summary: Planning and revision are intended to bring generated code closer to the task specification. Yet a mistaken interpretation can persist across the plan, implementation, and tests - a pattern we call interpretive lock-in. We investigate this risk on 30 DataFrame tasks derived from TPC Benchmark DS, comparing Frozen One-Pass, Test-Guided Revision, and PlanAudit-Guided Revision. Test-pass counts rose from 22/30 to 29/30 and 30/30, yet no generated solution matched its stored reference output. Evaluator controls returned the expected outcome in 57/57 cases. Same-engine SQL re-execution reproduced 28/30 references; all 77 test-passing runs on these tasks still failed reference agreement. PlanAudit-Guided Revision improved code scores on 3/30 tasks and test coverage on 11/30, but the median paired change was zero for both measures. Failure analysis revealed tests that omitted requirements, adopted candidate-defined schemas, used nondiscriminating fixtures, or repeated the implementation's incorrect logic. Fresh generation on ten targeted tasks produced 0/30 reference matches and 25/25 false passes among test-passing runs. These findings are diagnostic rather than causal: the pipelines differ in feedback, grounding, call budgets, and editing permissions, and the study uses one model and one primary generation per eligible task. Because pre-adjudication human labels were not retained, inter-rater agreement cannot be reconstructed and the mechanism analyses remain exploratory. Overall, increasingly successful self-generated tests did not establish semantic correctness, even after excluding unreproduced references.
Software Engineering.comment: Accepted at the International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering Researches (ICECER 2026)

Software Engineering.title: A Decade in a Day: Synthesizing Agent-Native Interfaces from Human-Oriented Software Evolution
Software Engineering.summary: Large language model agents are emerging as an important new class of users of desktop applications. However, existing desktop interfaces were designed for human end users or application developers, leaving agents to interpret visual controls or discover and compose low-level software operations. This mismatch can hinder even capable agents, yet it remains unclear what interface properties make desktop software easier for agents to use.
